short: The telephone information and referral line for local help. Madison County's calls are answered in Huntsville and Cullman County's from Birmingham.
def: 2-1-1 is an information and referral line answered by regional call centers, each serving a set of counties
. The Huntsville center, the 2-1-1 HELPline, serves DeKalb, Limestone, Jackson, Madison, Marshall and Morgan counties
. Cullman County's calls are answered by 2-1-1 Central Alabama in Birmingham
. Crisis Services of North Alabama says it manages 2-1-1 for the six counties of the Huntsville center

short: A public corporation formed under Alabama's Act 310 of 1967 to contract with the Department of Mental Health. WellStone is the 310 board for mental illness in both counties.
def: Act 310 provides for public corporations to be formed to contract with the Department of Mental Health in building facilities and running mental health programs; the bodies formed under it are commonly called 310 boards
. The Department says community mental health centers are governed by 310 boards
. WellStone says it was incorporated in 1969 as a result of the act

. Three 310-board plans are on file with the Department for the two counties: WellStone's, for mental illness and substance use, and one each from the Madison County 310 Board and the Cullman County 310 Authority for intellectual disability services

short: The national three-digit number for a mental health or suicide crisis. One of Alabama's four in-state call centers is at WellStone in Huntsville.
def: 988 is the national number for a mental health or suicide crisis, reachable by call, text or chat at any hour
. Alabama has four in-state call centers, in Mobile, Birmingham, Dothan and Huntsville, and the Huntsville one is at WellStone

. The Department of Mental Health's page publishes no list of the counties each center answers; WellStone said in April 2024 that a Cullman County caller reaches the Huntsville center, which connects the caller to a local crisis team

. The Department's table for fiscal year 2025 gives the WellStone center 6,627 of a four-center total of 35,118, and the Department gave it $660,000 of opioid settlement money to expand staffing and hours

short: The homelessness continuum of care that covers 37 Alabama counties, Cullman among them, from Montgomery. It publishes no county-level count.
def: The Alabama Balance of State continuum, numbered AL-507, was established in 2004 and serves 37 counties, Cullman among them; it is coordinated by the Alabama Rural Coalition for the Homeless in Montgomery
. Its own figures for 27 January 2026 are 636 people counted across the continuum, 72.3% of them unsheltered, with no county breakdown

. The only project with Cullman in its name in the 2025 federal housing inventory for the continuum is a 21-bed emergency shelter run by a domestic violence agency, and the inventory lists no permanent supportive housing project

term: Alabama Bureau of Pardons and Paroles (the parole bureau)
short: The state agency that supervises people on probation and parole. It runs a day reporting center in Huntsville.
def: The Bureau of Pardons and Paroles supervises people released to the community and operates the state's day reporting centers
. Huntsville's is one of five such centers
. In Cullman County the Bureau was named as a source of referrals to The Link's reentry program, which was due to begin enrolling in October 2020

term: Alabama Department of Mental Health (the Department)
short: The state agency for public mental health, substance use and developmental disability services. It certifies WellStone and names the counties each crisis center serves.
def: The Department of Mental Health is the state mental health authority: it operates the state psychiatric hospitals, certifies and contracts with community providers, and administers federal grants and the clinic demonstration
. WellStone states that it is certified by the Department, and the Department's county list names it as the center for Madison and Cullman
. The Department also publishes the list of counties each crisis center serves, and keeps a Region I Community Services office in Decatur

short: The state public health agency, separate from the Department of Mental Health. It keeps the statistics on deaths, including suicides and overdoses.
def: The Alabama Department of Public Health is the state public health agency; it is separate from the Department of Mental Health and publishes the state's vital statistics
. It publishes the explanation of federal shortage designations used in this report and a county-by-county list of public transport options

. Its county-level deaths by cause, race and sex are published only inside statewide documents of several hundred pages and through an online query system, with no short county table of suicides or drug poisonings for Madison or Cullman
. A community conversation it held in Huntsville for the 2025 State Health Assessment recorded knowledge about resources, an aging community and chronic disease as the three biggest concerns

short: The state's juvenile justice agency. It holds young people committed by juvenile courts and funds local diversion programs, including grants in Madison and Cullman counties.
def: The Department of Youth Services is Alabama's juvenile justice agency: it holds young people committed by juvenile courts and funds local diversion programs
. Its September 2026 reference book lists a diversion grant in Madison County with 47 slots, whose services include in-home crisis intervention and counseling for young people and their families
. Cullman County's diversion grant has eight slots, and WellStone runs a 15-slot after-school program there, funded as an Our Kids grant
. The same book lists a 110-day residential program for boys aged 12 to 18 that serves Cullman among sixteen counties

term: Alabama Opioid Overdose and Addiction Council
short: The state council that reports each year on opioid overdose and addiction in Alabama, including where naloxone has been distributed.
def: The Alabama Opioid Overdose and Addiction Council issues an annual report, which the Alabama Department of Mental Health posts
. Its 2025 report lists the counties with the highest distribution of naloxone, each with more than 1,300 doses, and Madison is among them at 2,344
. It also describes a statewide mail-order naloxone program run by the Jefferson County Department of Health
. No mention of Cullman County was found in the report

short: Alabama's Children's Health Insurance Program. With its Medicaid expansion group it covered 12,741 children in Madison County and 4,757 in Cullman County in July 2026.
def: The state health department's county table splits Children's Health Insurance Program enrollment into ALL Kids, for children at 146% to 317% of the federal poverty level, and a Medicaid expansion group at 100% to 145%
. In July 2026 the two groups together covered 12,741 children in Madison County and 4,757 in Cullman County
. A year earlier the counts were 11,337 and 4,462

term: Alternative Court (Madison County's juvenile specialty courts)
short: Madison County's juvenile mental health docket, one of three specialty courts in its juvenile court alongside a drug court and a truancy court.
def: Madison County's juvenile court has three specialty courts: a drug court, the Alternative Court and a truancy court

. The county describes them as judicially supervised treatment programs for nonviolent offenders, combining substance abuse and mental health treatment with case management, drug testing and probation supervision
. The Alternative Court was founded by a circuit judge to address the mental health needs of juveniles, and the court's site calls it the first of its kind in Alabama
. The county's page gives no providers, eligibility rules or numbers

short: The Census Bureau's continuous household survey. Its five-year estimates are the only survey figures published for areas as small as a census tract.
def: The regional map's tract layers on population, income, insurance, housing and similar subjects come from the Census Bureau's data-profile tables for the 2020-2024 American Community Survey, retrieved for the 117 census tracts of Madison and Cullman counties, the two counties and Alabama
. They are sample estimates for small areas, so many tract values have wide margins of error
. The values are not used in the report's text

short: The share of 988 calls from Alabama answered by a counselor in the state instead of rolling over to a national backup center.
def: The in-state answer rate is the share of 988 calls from Alabama that a counselor in Alabama answers; a call that no Alabama center picks up passes to a national backup

. The Alabama Department of Mental Health's board was told in November 2025 that the state's answering rate had been above 90% since July 2025, against a federal goal of 80% and the Department's own goal of 90%
. The Department's 988 page names the Huntsville call center at WellStone and gives no answer rate for it
. The measure says nothing about what happened after a call was answered

short: Legal permission to spend a set amount of public money in a given year, granted by a legislature, council or commission. It is made one year at a time.
def: In state budgeting an appropriation is the Legislature's legal permission for an agency to spend a set amount of public money in a given year; it is made a year at a time, so a program funded once has no claim on the next year's budget
. City councils make them too: the City of Huntsville's budget for fiscal year 2026 allotted $900,000 to WellStone, of which the council moved $36,000 to another agency by amendment
. The City of Madison's appropriation to WellStone for fiscal year 2024, as proposed on its council agenda of 23 October 2023, was $45,000
. Huntsville's release on its fiscal year 2027 budget gives totals for outside agencies and names no agency

short: A regional body designated by the state to plan and run services for older people. Madison and Cullman counties fall under different ones.
def: An area agency on aging serves a named group of counties, and a state guide lists each agency with its counties

. Madison County's sits in the Top of Alabama Regional Council of Governments, which is designated by the State of Alabama to develop and administer an area plan for aging in five counties and lists mental health services among the things older people most need

. Cullman County's is the North Central Alabama Regional Council of Governments, based in Decatur, which serves Cullman, Lawrence and Morgan counties and helps Medicare beneficiaries apply for benefits that cover premiums and prescription costs
. The fifteen counties of the crisis center's catchment are spread across six such agencies

short: Court-ordered treatment in the community for a person who has been through the commitment process; in Madison County, run by the probate court with WellStone since 2020.
def: Assisted outpatient treatment is court-ordered outpatient care for people with severe mental illness who can live safely in the community with treatment and have had trouble staying in it voluntarily
. Madison County's probate court announced its program with WellStone, to start on 3 February 2020, paying for it at first from the passport application fees the court collects
. A person enters only after a commitment petition, an assessment, a physician's confirmation that outpatient care is appropriate, a written treatment plan and a hearing
. As designed, participants have a case manager and a therapist and report every 30 days for up to 150 days
. A federal grant of $3,099,656 to WellStone, with the probate court and Huntsville Hospital as named partners, ran from 31 July 2022 to 30 July 2026 and set a target of 275 people enrolled

short: Counts of the beds a hospital is permitted to operate. The hospital association's figures cover a whole hospital and do not show how many of its beds are psychiatric.
def: The Alabama Hospital Association's listings give each hospital a number of authorized beds: 881 for Huntsville Hospital, 180 for Crestwood Medical Center and 175 for Cullman Regional Medical Center
. Audited statements speak of licensed beds, as when Decatur West is described as licensed for sixty-four psychiatric beds
. Neither the association's listing for Huntsville Hospital nor the hospital's own behavioral health page gives a count of psychiatric beds

short: WellStone's private fundraising campaign, launched in spring 2021, toward the cost of the crisis center and later the pediatric unit. Its page publishes no goal or total.
def: Be the Rock is the capital campaign WellStone launched in spring 2021 to raise funds for psychiatric crisis care for adults

. The crisis center was reported to cost $10 million, of which the campaign was to fund the remaining $5 million after state and local contributions; when the center opened, the campaign had raised close to $550,000
. WellStone also credits the campaign's supporters, with the Legislature and the Department of Mental Health, for the $9 million pediatric unit, without giving each share
. The campaign page publishes no goal, total or donor list, and in December 2024 WellStone's development director described the campaign as winding down

short: A private addiction treatment provider whose campus in the city of Madison offers medical detox, residential treatment and medication-assisted treatment.
def: Bradford Health Services' Madison campus, at 1600 Browns Ferry Road, offers on-site medical detox, residential treatment and medication-assisted treatment, with a recovery program for veterans
. The provider's page gives no bed count
. Two of the fourteen substance use entries in the Alabama Department of Mental Health's provider directory for Madison County are Bradford's

short: Cullman County's child advocacy center. It provides forensic interviews, counseling and medical exams at no cost to families and says it is funded entirely by local donations.
def: Brooks' Place is Cullman County's child advocacy center
. It provides forensic interviews, individual and family counseling, medical exams and community education at no cost to families
. It lists five staff, two of them therapists, and says all its funding comes from local donations
. Its service page gives no count of children served
. In Madison County the National Children's Advocacy Center in Huntsville offers forensic interviews, medical exams and trauma therapy

short: The state's psychiatric hospital for adults, in Tuscaloosa. An adult from north Alabama who is committed to a state bed is sent there.
def: Bryce Hospital in Tuscaloosa is the state hospital responsible for inpatient psychiatric services for adults throughout Alabama

. When North Alabama Regional Hospital was to close in 2015, the commissioner said its patients would be served by acute care units at hospitals, crisis stabilization units, intermediate care facilities run by community centers or, if necessary, Bryce
. The Alabama Department of Mental Health's page for the hospital gives no bed count, catchment or admission procedure, and says nothing about how patients are brought there
. State law has the probate judge order one or more persons or law enforcement officers to take a committed person to the facility the court names

short: Cullman County's only public transit: a county-run weekday service, 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., on which a ride must be booked by 2:30 p.m. the day before.
def: CARTS, the Cullman Area Rural Transportation System, is the county-run demand-response service that is Cullman County's only public transit
. It operates Monday to Friday from 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. with 37 vehicles, 36 of them equipped with accessible lifts
. Reservations must be made by 2:30 p.m. the previous business day, and the fare is $2 to $6 each way by distance

short: The set of counties a center is assigned to serve. It shows who is responsible for an area, not how far residents must travel or how much they use the center.
def: A catchment is the set of counties a facility is designated to serve; it is a measure of responsibility, and a resident of the catchment may still live hours away
. WellStone's strategic plan gives its catchment as the residents of Madison and Cullman counties
. The Department of Mental Health's Crisis Centers page lists fifteen counties as served by the Huntsville crisis center: those two and thirteen more
. The Department's annual report for fiscal year 2025 counts the people served at the crisis center with no breakdown by county of residence

term: CCBHC provider manual (the state's clinic manual)
short: The Department of Mental Health's rulebook for Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics: what they must provide, how they are paid and how they must be run.
def: The provider manual for Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) is the Alabama Department of Mental Health's manual for these clinics, and this report read version 1
. It names the payment method, a daily rate for all clinic services delivered each day to an enrolled Medicaid beneficiary, and says the rate is not paid for people outside Medicaid
. It expects telehealth to be used as far as possible to support access, and requires staff training in evidence-based practices and trauma-informed care among other subjects
. The edition for the third quarter of 2026 could not be read, so the earlier one was used

short: The results a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic must report: five measures the clinic collects itself and twelve the state calculates.
def: As a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic (CCBHC), WellStone must report five quality measures it collects itself: time to services, depression remission at six months, screening for unhealthy alcohol use, screening for social drivers of health, and depression screening with a follow-up plan
. The manual that sets these also sets twelve measures collected by the state
. Clinics must submit each measurement year's data by 30 September of the following year

. The Alabama Department of Mental Health's board minutes of May 2025 speak of 15 to 17 outcome measures specified at the federal level, record that the Department had invested in a platform called Netsmart to report on outcomes, and give no results

short: An annual report on clinic and state quality measures that the Department of Mental Health's manual says it will produce. None had appeared by 4 October 2026.
def: The Alabama Department of Mental Health's quality reporting manual for Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics (CCBHCs) says the Department "will also develop an annual CCBHC Quality Report" with detail on clinic and state-level quality measures
. The manual sets a reporting deadline of 30 September, and its rules bind WellStone as one of the state's clinics
. The statewide report found no such report published as of October 2026

short: A federal dataset of modeled health estimates for counties, cities and census tracts. Its tract values are produced by a model, not by surveying each tract.
def: PLACES is the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's set of model-based estimates of health measures for every census tract in the country
. The dataset's own description says the estimates draw on the 2023 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System, 2020 census population counts and American Community Survey estimates
. Ten of its measures for adults supply tract layers of the regional map; they are modeled values, not counts or survey results for each tract

short: The community mental health center for Cherokee, DeKalb and Etowah counties in northeast Alabama. One of the four centers that serve the ring.
def: CED Mental Health Center is the trading name of the Etowah-Cherokee-DeKalb Mental Health Board, which has served northeast Alabama since 1974 from one office in each of its three counties
. Its published crisis service is a 24-hour emergency telephone line
. It says it cared for approximately 4,576 consumers in fiscal year 2023–2024, and the Department of Mental Health's FY2025 report counts 2,558 people served
. It is not a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic, and its plan names transportation as a continuing need

short: The Census Bureau's summary profile of population, income, insurance and other figures for a county or city. Appendix A takes population, income and uninsured rates from it.
def: QuickFacts is the Census Bureau's profile of a county or city, giving population, age, race and Hispanic origin, veterans, disability, insurance, income and poverty
. Its population estimates for 1 July 2025 run from 13,587 in Lamar County to 433,516 in Madison County across the fifteen counties, with Cullman at 94,009
. Median household income for 2020–2024 is $86,499 in Madison and $62,656 in Cullman

short: A small area within a county for which statistics are published. The federal PLACES estimates of local health go down to this level.
def: A census tract is one of the areas below county level for which the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's PLACES project publishes model-based health estimates, alongside counties, places and ZIP Code tabulation areas
. No other public source of mental health estimates below county level was found for Huntsville, Madison and Cullman

term: Certificate of need (state approval for hospital beds)
short: The state's permission for a hospital to build or add beds. Alabama's review board approved a $150 million tower at Huntsville Hospital in November 2024.
def: On 20 November 2024 the Alabama Certificate of Need Review Board approved a five-story, $150 million addition to Huntsville Hospital's Madison Street Tower, which would take the hospital from 881 to 931 beds
. The hospital's announcement does not mention psychiatric beds; it reports an approval, with construction expected to take about two years
. For inpatient psychiatric beds, the State Health Plan's rule sets the regional method by which the need for more is judged

short: A clinic certified to provide a required set of mental health and substance use services to anyone who seeks care, and paid a daily rate by Medicaid. WellStone has been one since July 2024.
def: A Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic follows a federal clinic model: it must provide nine required services, among them round-the-clock crisis response and primary care screening, and Medicaid pays it a daily rate in place of fee-for-service
. Alabama's manual requires a clinic to provide the full array of services to everyone seeking care, regardless of ability to pay
. The state certified WellStone effective July 2024, and WellStone describes itself as one of the first two Alabama clinics in the Medicaid demonstration
. The Department of Mental Health's directory lists full-scope clinic sites at WellStone's Huntsville and Cullman campuses and at Mountain Lakes' offices in Guntersville and Scottsboro
. The Department counts 13,700 people served by WellStone as a clinic in fiscal year 2025

term: Children with an indication of abuse or neglect
short: A Kids Count measure: the number of children in a county with an indication of abuse or neglect in a year, also given as a rate per 1,000.
def: A row in the Kids Count county profiles, given as a count of children and as a rate per 1,000
. In 2024 Cullman County had 338 such children, a rate of 16.4 per 1,000 that ranked 53rd of Alabama's 67 counties
. Madison County had 325, a rate of 3.6 per 1,000 that ranked first
. The statewide figure was 11,482 children, or 10.1 per 1,000
. The Cullman profile prints no source line for the indicator

short: A subgroup reported in the federal homelessness count. The Huntsville continuum's January 2025 count listed 128 chronically homeless people.
def: Chronically homeless persons are one of the subgroups in the federal report of the point-in-time count
. The 2025 count for the Huntsville continuum lists 128, of whom 55 were in emergency shelter and 73 unsheltered
. The figure was 218 in 2023 and 71 in 2024
. The continuum had 190 permanent supportive housing beds in January 2025, for three counties

short: A court order requiring a person with mental illness to accept treatment. In Alabama the county probate court hears the petition; it is not a criminal matter.
def: Civil commitment is involuntary treatment ordered by a court outside the criminal process; in Alabama any person may petition the probate court, and the judge may order inpatient treatment on clear and convincing evidence that the legal standard is met

. In Madison County, as the probate judge described it in May 2025, a person held on an intent to commit has a hearing at about the third or fourth day and by then is at Huntsville Hospital or WellStone
. The judge said an inpatient commitment lasts up to 150 days and can be renewed to 300, which the judge called very rare because of bed availability

. The only yearly figures come from press reports and count different things: over 300 people committed in 2019, 309 petitions in 2019 and 414 in 2021, and a peak of 589 involuntary commitments in 2023
. Cullman County's probate court publishes no commitment procedure, forms or counts on its web page

short: The record behind the report: every claim it makes, the passage that supports it, and whether it is verified, the report's own analysis, or a statement that something was not found.
def: The claims ledger lists each claim in the report with the words that state it, the source passage that supports it, and a status. A claim is verified against a quoted passage, or is the report's own analysis or arithmetic, or records that something was not found, or is a statement about the report itself. The reader shows these statuses on request, and a bracketed number in the text opens the supporting passage.

short: A police program in which a mental health clinician rides with an officer on calls involving a person in crisis. Huntsville's followed a council vote in May 2021.
def: Co-responder programs pair police officers with mental health clinicians on calls involving a person in crisis; a mobile crisis team, unlike a co-responder, is sent without police

. The Huntsville City Council voted on 13 May 2021 to support a partnership of the City, its police and WellStone, planned around two full-time master's-level clinicians working from 2 p.m. to midnight
. By February 2022 two clinicians were riding with the department's crisis intervention officers
. The City's account of the program gives no counts of calls or outcomes

term: Commercial insurance (employer coverage and Blue Cross)
variants: Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Alabama
short: Private health insurance, most often obtained through a job. Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Alabama held 82% of the Huntsville area's commercial market at the start of 2024.
def: Commercial insurance is sold by private companies to employers and individuals
. Census survey estimates for 2024, as an aggregator presents them, put 53.2% of Madison County residents and 41.9% of Cullman County residents on employer plans

. In the Huntsville metropolitan area Blue Cross and Blue Shield of Alabama held 82% of the commercial health insurance market as of 1 January 2024, with the second insurer at 5%, according to the American Medical Association
. The chief executive of the Huntsville Hospital system told the city council in April 2026 that the system negotiates with that single commercial insurer

short: Locally run programs that supervise people convicted of crimes in the community as an alternative to prison. Madison County's is a public authority; Cullman County's is a nonprofit.
def: Community corrections programs supervise convicted people locally, under contract with the Alabama Department of Corrections, and form Intercept 5 of the Sequential Intercept Model
. The Department describes them as local supervision that includes evidence-based treatment programs and services
. Its map of 1 April 2023 labels Madison's program as an authority serving the 23rd Judicial Circuit and Cullman's as a nonprofit serving the 32nd

. Madison County's program lets people who are incarcerated or facing incarceration serve all or the rest of a sentence at an approved home plan in the county, and Cullman's is based in the county courthouse

short: A free clinic in Huntsville for uninsured Madison County residents, with an on-site dispensary where prescriptions are filled. It lists no mental health service.
def: The Community Free Clinic of Huntsville/Madison County, at 410 Sivley Road SW, serves Madison County residents who are uninsured and not covered by Medicaid or Medicare
. It fills prescriptions from an on-site dispensary, opens three days a week and lists no mental health service
. In Cullman County, United Way's funding list for 2022–23 describes the Good Samaritan Health Clinic as providing health care and prescriptions for uninsured, low-income residents

short: A periodic local study of a community's health needs. Cullman Regional publishes one for Cullman County; Madison County's nearest equivalent is a 2024 United Way assessment.
def: Cullman Regional Medical Center has published a community health needs assessment for Cullman County every three years since 2013, the latest in 2025
. The 2025 assessment rests on an online survey of 47 community representatives and on secondary data; 62.2% of those surveyed rated mental health a major problem
. In Madison County, United Way ran a community needs survey from 15 May to 30 June 2024 with a team from Alabama A&M University

. Its executive summary names transportation, environmental pollution and recycling, and services for abused and neglected children as the areas residents most often said needed improvement; mental health appears as a recommendation

short: One of the regional organizations that deliver public outpatient mental health care in Alabama. WellStone is the center for Madison and Cullman counties.
def: Alabama delivers public mental health care through community mental health centers, which the Department of Mental Health calls "the designated points of entry" for mental health and substance use services and which are governed by 310 boards
. The Department's page lists 19 centers, which the statewide report describes as together covering all 67 counties

. The Department's county list gives Madison and Cullman to WellStone and the thirteen ring counties to four other centers: Mountain Lakes, the Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama, CED and Northwest Alabama
. Under Alabama Medicaid's rule, a provider of rehabilitative mental health services must be certified by the Department as a 310-board community mental health center

short: A sheriff's deputy appointed by the Madison County probate judge, with more than 80 hours of crisis training, to respond to people in a mental health crisis.
def: In August 2020 the Madison County probate judge appointed members of the Sheriff's Office as Community Mental Health Officers
. Each had completed more than 80 hours of crisis training, and they were described as the front-line response for people experiencing a mental health crisis
. The report of the appointments does not say how many were appointed
. In a Madison County commitment case the probate judge orders the Sheriff to serve the patient with notice of the hearing

short: Treatment meant to make a defendant who was found incompetent able to stand trial. It is given at the state forensic hospital or, in seven Alabama counties, inside the jail.
def: Competency restoration is treatment aimed at making a defendant able to take part in a trial; it is a legal goal and not the same as recovery
. Jail-based restoration delivers the treatment inside a county jail, so that a defendant does not have to wait for a state hospital bed
. The Department of Mental Health's FY2025 report names seven counties whose jails offer it: DeKalb, Fayette, Jefferson, Mobile, Pickens, Shelby and Walker
. Neither Madison nor Cullman is among them, though DeKalb, Fayette and Walker are ring counties

short: A defendant's ability to understand the proceedings and help in their own defense. A person found incompetent cannot be tried until competency is restored.
def: A person cannot be tried while unable to take part in their own defense, and when the question is raised the court orders an evaluation
. A defendant found incompetent must be given treatment aimed at restoring competency before the case can go ahead
. In Alabama that has mostly meant waiting in a county jail for a bed at the state's forensic hospital
. The press reports of that wait give state totals and name no north Alabama county

short: A 2025 Alabama law raised from 14 to 16 the age below which a student needs a parent's written permission for ongoing school counseling.
def: A 2025 state law raised the age of independent consent for medical and mental health treatment from 14 to 16, effective 1 October 2025
. In schools it means that a student under 16 cannot take part in ongoing counseling without a parent's written opt-in
. Cullman City Schools' page states the new rule
. Madison County Schools' opt-in page, as read, still gave the threshold as students under 14

short: A regional body, recognized by the federal housing department, that plans the local response to homelessness and runs the yearly count. Madison and Cullman are in different ones.
def: A Continuum of Care is a regional body that coordinates housing and services for homeless people in its area, runs the point-in-time count and sets priorities for federal homelessness grants; despite the name it is an organization and not a range of services
. Madison County is in the continuum run by the North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless, numbered AL-503, with Limestone and Morgan counties
. Cullman County is not named in that or any other regional continuum on the state's list, which leaves it in the balance-of-state continuum, AL-507
. The federal reports of the count for AL-503 give 549 homeless people in 2022 and 718 in 2025

short: A homelessness continuum's shared entry process for people seeking help. In the Huntsville continuum it is held in person at the Downtown Rescue Mission.
def: In-person coordinated entry for the Huntsville continuum is held at the Downtown Rescue Mission, Monday to Thursday from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
. Family Services Center in Huntsville holds the federal grant for the continuum's supportive services and coordinated entry project, $84,554 for FY2024
. The Downtown Rescue Mission also supplies 200 of the continuum's 421 emergency shelter beds

short: The county official whose office investigates deaths. Local counts of suicides and overdoses come from coroners and reach the public mainly through news interviews.
def: The coroner's office investigates deaths in a county; Madison County's runs a nine-week training program for new death investigators
. Its website publishes no statistics: no annual report and no counts of suicides or overdose deaths
. The Madison County coroner's figures reach the public through interviews, such as a projection of 16 fatal overdoses for June 2021 against a usual six to eight a month
. The Cullman County coroner counted 17 suicide deaths in 2022 and 22 in 2021, as the local paper reported

short: A national publication of county health measures. This report uses its rural share, provider ratios, and suicide and overdose death rates for the fifteen counties.
def: County Health Rankings is the source of several county measures used in this report, taken from the county file already checked for the statewide report
. It counts 17.1% of Madison County's population and 75.6% of Cullman County's as living in a rural area
. Its March 2026 supplement gives age-adjusted suicide rates for 2019 to 2023 of 15.3 per 100,000 in Madison County and 20.7 in Cullman County, and 474 and 568 residents per mental health provider

. Its rates pool several years, so they need not match another publisher's: Cullman County's drug overdose death rate is 35.6 per 100,000 here, for 2021 to 2023, and 26.4 in the local hospital's assessment, for 2018 to 2022

short: Adults who earn too much for Alabama's Medicaid and too little for subsidized marketplace insurance. Alabama has not expanded Medicaid, and no county estimate of the gap was found.
def: The Affordable Care Act let states extend Medicaid to adults with incomes up to 138% of the federal poverty level, and Alabama is one of the states that has not done so
. In such a state some adults fall between two programs: their income is above the state's Medicaid limit and below the poverty line, where marketplace subsidies begin
. A 2022 economic analysis put the statewide expansion population at 283,636 people and, as read, gives no county-level estimate of the gap

short: A place open at all hours where a person in a mental health crisis can walk in or be brought by police or ambulance, as an alternative to an emergency room or jail.
def: The Department of Mental Health describes its crisis centers as open around the clock to people who walk in and to those brought by law enforcement, first responders or emergency medical crews
. Alabama has six, and the Department's map shows seven counties covered by none
. The Huntsville center, run by WellStone, was one of the first three the state named, on 28 October 2020, from an $18 million appropriation

. The state's evaluation office reported in 2025 that each of the six centers was funded at $7,000,000 a year; it found the centers' monthly reports inconsistent and published no count of jail or emergency room avoidance for any single center

term: Crisis intervention training (Crisis Intervention Team, CIT)
short: Training that prepares police officers to respond to people in a mental health crisis. Huntsville Police is the training hub for an 18-county north Alabama region.
def: Crisis Intervention Team programs are partnerships of law enforcement, mental health providers and families, built around a 40-hour training course for officers

. NAMI Alabama's plan for the training names WellStone Emergency Services, the Huntsville Police Department and NAMI Huntsville as the program for its Region 1, which covers eighteen north Alabama counties including Madison and Cullman
. In May 2021 Huntsville Police had 75 officers certified through the 40-hour course, and the City said then that all its officers attend a 16-hour course
. No count of officers trained appears in NAMI Alabama's plan or on its list of regional hubs

short: A small staffed residence where a person in crisis can stay for a short period as an alternative to a hospital ward.
def: A crisis residential unit is a small staffed residence where a person in crisis can stay for a short period as an alternative to a hospital ward, and the Alabama Department of Mental Health counts such beds at certified providers among its beds for people under civil commitment
. The Department's directory entry for WellStone Emergency Services lists crisis residential care among the services offered there

. The civil commitment and crisis residential beds the Department funded from the third round of opioid settlement money are in Blount, Escambia and Chambers counties and at one further unit, and none is in Madison or Cullman County
. In the ring, Northwest Alabama Mental Health Center operates a 16-bed unit for adults at Townley in Walker County that takes referrals statewide

. At a groundbreaking on 10 December 2024 the Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama described a 16-bed unit in Decatur for people committed to the Department, with construction expected to be complete by October 2025

short: An organization that runs a 24-hour crisis counseling line, a domestic violence shelter and sexual assault services, and manages 2-1-1 for Madison and five nearby counties.
def: Crisis Services of North Alabama runs a confidential 24-hour crisis counseling line called the HELPline, the HOPE Place emergency shelter for victims of domestic violence, and sexual assault support that includes forensic exams
. It serves victims of domestic violence and sexual assault in Madison, Morgan, Limestone and Jackson counties, and provides sexual assault response in Cullman and Winston counties
. It manages 2-1-1 for Jackson, Limestone, Madison, Morgan, Marshall and DeKalb counties; Cullman is not on that list
. The City of Madison's council agenda of 23 October 2023 carried a $15,000 appropriation to it for fiscal year 2024

short: The services for a mental health emergency: a line to call, a team that comes, and a place to go that is neither an emergency room nor a jail.
def: Federal guidance describes a crisis system as three essential elements: someone to contact, someone to respond, and a safe place for help
. In this region the Department lists WellStone Emergency Services and WellStone Pediatric Crisis Care at one Huntsville address, serving fifteen counties

short: Cullman County's hospital. It offers outpatient psychiatry and a behavioral health area in its emergency room, has no inpatient psychiatric unit, and publishes the county's needs assessment.
def: The hospital association lists Cullman Regional Medical Center with 175 authorized beds, and the only psychiatric service in the listing is outpatient
. Its emergency department expansion, completed in July 2022, includes a dedicated behavioral health treatment area
. Its 2025 community health needs assessment ranks mental health first and substance use second among thirteen areas of opportunity
. The implementation plan its board adopted on 11 March 2025 takes on mental health as one of seven needs, and substance use is not among the seven

short: The fixed amount Medicaid pays a certified clinic for each day it gives a Medicaid enrollee a qualifying service, whatever the service. It is not paid for people outside Medicaid.
def: "Prospective" means the rate is fixed ahead of time from the clinic's expected costs and is not billed item by item afterwards
. Under Alabama's billing manual a clinic receives a single payment for each day on which at least one qualifying service is provided to a Medicaid enrollee
. Each clinic's rate is rebuilt from its actual costs and visits after its second demonstration year and every three years after that
. The provider manual says the rate "will not be paid for services provided to populations outside of those enrolled in Medicaid"
. No daily rate for WellStone appears in its strategic plan

short: A facility where people on probation or parole who are judged high-risk report for supervision and treatment while living at home. One of Alabama's five is in Huntsville.
def: A day reporting center is a facility of the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles for high-risk probationers and parolees, with contracted mental health and substance use treatment
. The centers address education, employment, substance abuse, mental health and what the Bureau calls cognitive restructuring, in a three-phase program with required community service
. Huntsville's is one of five; the others are in Birmingham, Mobile, Montgomery and Tuscaloosa

term: Days to first evaluation (wait for a first appointment)
short: The number of days a new patient waits for an initial assessment. At WellStone it fell from 18 days in January 2025 to under one day in December 2025.
def: The measure is the number of days to a patient's initial evaluation, which the Department of Mental Health also calls an assessment
. The Department told legislators in January 2026 that at WellStone it was 18 days in January 2025 and less than one day in December 2025
. A companion measure, days to a first therapy session, went from 33 to eight over the same months
. These are the only access-time figures published for WellStone

short: A hospital campus in Decatur, Morgan County, licensed for 64 psychiatric beds and used mainly for children and adolescents. It lies outside Madison and Cullman counties.
def: Decatur Morgan Hospital West, in neighboring Morgan County, is described by the Huntsville Hospital Health System as north Alabama's only behavioral health hospital, with 64 licensed beds for inpatient and outpatient psychiatric programs primarily for children and adolescents

. The audited statements of the system's parent authority for the year to 30 June 2025 describe it as licensed for sixty-four psychiatric beds and give no count of psychiatric beds at Huntsville Hospital itself

. Before WellStone's pediatric unit opened it was described as the nearest psychiatric hospital for adolescents, and about 400 of the roughly 800 young people reported to be taken out of Madison County each year went there

short: Public transport that runs on booked trips instead of a fixed route: the rider reserves a ride in advance.
def: A demand-response service carries riders on trips reserved in advance, and the two rural services in this report, CARTS in Cullman County and TRAM in Madison County, both work this way
. CARTS requires a reservation by 2:30 p.m. the previous business day, and TRAM a booking 24 hours in advance and before 3 p.m. the day before
. Huntsville's Orbit, by comparison, is a bus system with published weekday and Saturday hours and a $1 fare

short: Alabama's child welfare agency, responsible for child protection and foster care, with a county office in each of Madison and Cullman counties.
def: The Alabama Department of Human Resources is the state's child welfare agency, responsible for child protection and foster care, and it also administers the SNAP food benefit
. Its county offices are in Huntsville for Madison County and in Cullman for Cullman County
. The child and adolescent mobile crisis teams that WellStone runs in both counties are funded by the state in partnership with it
. It also has a seat on the team that reviews child abuse cases at the National Children's Advocacy Center

short: Medically supervised withdrawal from alcohol or drugs, the first step of treatment. River Crossing is WellStone's 16-bed detox unit in Huntsville, opened on 24 June 2025.
def: Detoxification is medically supervised withdrawal from alcohol or drugs; it is the first step of treatment, not the whole of it

. WellStone won the Department of Mental Health's request for proposals for a 16-bed residential detox program for adults with opioid, benzodiazepine or alcohol use disorder, renovated an existing facility and opened it on 24 June 2025
. The Department's annual report calls the unit River Crossing Withdrawal Management and says it is funded through a grant from the state's Opioid Settlement Fund
. The Department's slide describing the program prints no dollar amount

term: Disability waivers (Medicaid waivers for developmental disabilities)
short: Medicaid waivers for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, run by the Department of Mental Health. The statewide waiting list stood at 1,800 people in May 2025.
def: Medicaid waivers administered by the developmental disabilities division of the Alabama Department of Mental Health
. The division told the Department's board in May 2025 that the statewide waiting list for them had grown to 1,800 people
. Developmental disability services are funded largely by Medicaid and make up more than half of the Department's budget
. In Madison County a separate board is described as the single point of entry for people with intellectual disabilities who seek waiver services

short: Steering a person away from jail or an emergency room and into care. It is the stated purpose of the crisis center, and no count of people diverted there has been published.
def: Diversion means steering a person away from a costlier or more harmful setting, such as jail or an emergency room, and into care or a community program; counting one requires a judgment about what would have happened otherwise
. WellStone's chief executive described the main purpose of the crisis center's beds in October 2022 as "to divert individuals from our jails and our emergency departments"
. WellStone's jail diversion program in Madison County began about February 2018 and, some 90 days in, had moved 20 low-level offenders out of the jail with two case managers
. The state's 2025 evaluation of the crisis centers publishes no per-center counts of jail or emergency room avoidance

short: A free, voluntary community space for people with mental illness, outside clinical care. The state lists one in north Alabama, in Huntsville, and none in Cullman County.
def: The Department of Mental Health describes drop-in centers as free and voluntary community spaces that offer purpose and connection outside clinical care; some stand alone and others are run through local mental health providers
. It lists five in Alabama, and the only one in north Alabama is Our Place, on Max Luther Drive in Huntsville
. None is listed in Cullman County

short: Deaths from drug overdose for every 100,000 residents. Two sources give different figures for Cullman County, 35.6 and 26.4, for different periods.
def: A rate divides a count by population so that places of different size can be compared; overdose deaths are given per 100,000 residents
. County Health Rankings' March 2026 figures give drug overdose death rates of 29.1 in Madison County and 35.6 in Cullman County
. Cullman Regional's 2025 assessment gives Cullman County 26.4 as an annual average for 2018 to 2022, against 22.0 for Alabama and 26.9 for the United States
. A rate built on few events will swing from year to year, so the period matters when two figures are compared

short: The framework this report shares with the statewide report: eight domains of a mental health system, followed by four sections on systems outside the Department of Mental Health.
def: The statewide report describes Alabama's mental health system in eight domains and four cross-sector sections, and it supplies the frame used in this report

. Six of the domains follow the World Health Organization's building blocks of a health system: service delivery, health workforce, health information systems, access to essential medicines, financing, and leadership and governance
. The statewide report adds two domains of its own, on equity and on community engagement, and four further sections on children, justice, social determinants and payers

short: Holding a psychiatric patient in an emergency room, sometimes for days, because no inpatient bed or placement is available.
def: Boarding means holding a psychiatric patient in an emergency room because no inpatient bed or placement is available, and it is a sign that the levels of care beyond the emergency room are full
. No statewide measure of it was found in the Alabama Department of Mental Health's published reports as of October 2026
. Before WellStone's pediatric unit opened, children in Madison County were reported to wait in emergency rooms for as long as 24 hours for a psychiatric bed

short: A benchmark rent for an area. The report cites the hourly wage needed to afford a two-bedroom home at that rent: $25.19 in the Huntsville area and $17.94 in Cullman County.
def: The National Low Income Housing Coalition's Out of Reach report for 2026 gives fair market rents and the hourly wage a full-time worker must earn to afford a two-bedroom rental in each area
. For the Huntsville metropolitan area the two-bedroom fair market rent is $1,310 a month and the wage needed is $25.19 an hour
. For Cullman County the figures are $933 and $17.94

short: An organization accredited within the Alabama Network of Family Resource Centers. The Link of Cullman County became the state's 28th in September 2026.
def: The Link of Cullman County became Alabama's 28th accredited family resource center in September 2026, joining the Alabama Network of Family Resource Centers
. Its director described the reasoning this way: "A family that comes to us needing food may also be struggling with housing, employment, parenting, education or recovery"
. The Link has served Cullman County since 2013

term: Federal loan repayment (National Health Service Corps)
short: A federal program that repays clinicians' student loans in return for at least two years of work at an approved site in a shortage area.
def: The National Health Service Corps is a federal program that repays student loans for licensed behavioral health providers who work at an approved site in a mental health shortage area for at least two years
. As the Alabama Department of Public Health describes it, awards range from $30,000 to $75,000 for two years of full-time service and are tied to the shortage score
. The disciplines covered include psychiatrists, psychologists, licensed clinical social workers, licensed professional counselors and marriage and family therapists
. Cullman County's whole-county designation carries a score of 16, and Madison County has no area designation
. The department's page gives no count of Corps clinicians or sites in the two counties

short: The national list of health care providers' identifier numbers, used to count mental health providers by county. It can include people no longer practicing.
def: The National Plan and Provider Enumeration System, or NPPES, is the registry of National Provider Identifiers, and Cullman Regional's assessment credits it to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services

. County Health Rankings takes its mental health provider count from it, counting psychiatrists, psychologists, licensed clinical social workers, counselors, marriage and family therapists, providers who treat alcohol and other drug abuse, and advanced practice nurses specializing in mental health
. Cullman Regional's assessment uses the same registry with a different list: psychiatrists, psychologists, clinical social workers and counselors who specialize in mental health care
. Providers are assigned to counties by the ZIP code of their registered address, and some of those listed may no longer be practicing or accepting new patients

term: Federally designated health center (federally qualified health center)
short: A federally funded community clinic that provides primary care to anyone, with fees scaled to income. HAPPI Health has four sites, all in Huntsville.
def: Federally qualified health centers are federally funded nonprofit clinics that serve medically underserved areas and populations and adjust their fees to income
. HAPPI Health describes itself as designated by the federal Health Resources and Services Administration and lists four sites, all in Huntsville, with a sliding fee scale for uninsured patients
. Its behavioral health service offers therapy, mental health evaluations, substance use assessments and crisis intervention by licensed counselors and clinical social workers
. It lists no site in Cullman County

short: A Huntsville nonprofit serving homeless people. It received $810,000 of the city's first opioid settlement allocations and was named as one of the first stops for WellStone's mobile clinic.
def: First Stop is a Huntsville nonprofit that provides services to homeless people
. The City of Huntsville names it among its partner agencies on homelessness, and gave it $810,000 in the first opioid settlement allocations it announced in 2023
. WellStone's mobile clinic, announced in November 2025, started with First Stop and the Downtown Rescue Mission
. In March 2026 First Stop said it was tracking about 20 homeless encampments across Madison County and estimated that to be about half of those that exist

short: Team-based early treatment for young people having a first psychotic episode. WellStone runs NOVA-Huntsville, one of Alabama's three such programs.
def: A first-episode psychosis program is team-based early treatment for young people having a first psychotic episode, combining therapy, medication, family support, help with work or school and case management
. The Alabama Department of Mental Health operates three sites: NOVA-Birmingham, NOVA-Mobile and NOVA-Huntsville, the last at WellStone in Madison County

. Its page lists multi-family groups, youth and parent peer support, supported employment and education, care coordination, cognitive behavioral therapy and low-dose antipsychotic medication as needed
. The page gives no caseload for any site

short: A budget year, named for the year in which it ends. Alabama's runs from 1 October to 30 September, and WellStone's also ends in September.
def: Alabama's fiscal year runs from 1 October to 30 September and is named for the year in which it ends, so FY2025 means October 2024 to September 2025
. WellStone's financial years also end in September
. Not every body in this report keeps the same year: the Huntsville Hospital system's audit covers a year ended 30 June, and the clinic demonstration years run from 1 July to 30 June
. A figure for a fiscal year and a figure for a calendar year therefore overlap only in part

short: A measure of continuity: the share of people who see a mental health provider soon after leaving a psychiatric hospital. No result for WellStone is published.
def: Follow-up after hospitalization is the share of people who see a mental health provider within a set period of leaving a psychiatric hospital; the statewide report uses a seven-day version and notes that the first week after discharge is when people most often fall out of treatment
. It is among the measures set for Alabama's Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics
. Federal rules specify 15 to 17 outcome measures for these clinics, and the Alabama Department of Mental Health's board minutes of May 2025 give no results
. At the opening of the Huntsville crisis center, people leaving were to be assigned a care manager who would see that they reached their follow-up appointments

short: An interview, by a specialist at a child advocacy center, of a child who may have been abused or may have witnessed a crime or violent incident.
def: The National Children's Advocacy Center offers forensic interviews for children who may have been abused or who have witnessed a crime or violent incident

. Child forensic interview specialists sit on its multidisciplinary team with the district attorney's office, law enforcement, the Department of Human Resources, family advocates, therapists and medical professionals
. The center reported 488 forensic interviews in 2024, with 991 team case reviews and 129 forensic medical exams
. Brooks' Place provides forensic interviews in Cullman County

short: The Internal Revenue Service form on which a nonprofit reports its yearly revenue, expenses and assets. WellStone's latest on the public record is for the year ending September 2021.
def: Form 990 is the Internal Revenue Service form from which a public database, ProPublica's Nonprofit Explorer, shows a nonprofit's revenue, expenses and assets year by year
. The most recent year shown for WellStone is the one ending September 2021: revenue of $25,940,539, expenses of $20,991,369 and net assets of $17,628,969
. For the years ending September 2022 to 2025 the database lists federal single-audit records and no Form 990 data, and it flags the 2025 audit with a significant deficiency in internal controls
. The audit documents themselves could not be opened

short: The placement of a child, by the child welfare agency, away from the family home: with relatives, with foster parents or in a facility.
def: Foster care is the placement of a child by the child welfare agency away from the family home, with relatives, with foster parents or in a facility
. Kids Count counts 411 Madison County children in foster care in 2025, up from 252 in 2014, and 112 in Cullman County, down from 159
. Statewide the count rose from 5,009 to 5,813 over the same years
. Local providers include Kids to Love in Madison, which runs a child placing agency and a home for girls, and Childhaven in Cullman, which states its capacity as 32 residents

short: The military clinic on Redstone Arsenal. Its behavioral health department serves service members, families, retirees and civilian employees on weekdays.
def: Fox Army Health Center is the military clinic on Redstone Arsenal, and its behavioral health department offers psychotherapy, medication management, group treatment and evaluations
. The department says it serves active duty personnel, their family members, retirees and their family members, commanders and civilian employees, and no referral is needed
. When it cannot provide the care needed, and it gives a child and adolescent psychiatrist as the example, patients are offered care off post through TRICARE
. For emergencies after hours its page sends patients to the nearest emergency room or to WellStone Emergency Services

short: A federal estimate of the share of a county's adults who report frequent mental distress: 18.9% in Cullman County and 16.0% in Madison County in 2023.
def: One of the adult health measures that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention estimates at county level through its PLACES program
. The figures are model-based estimates published with confidence limits
. For 2023 the estimate is 18.9% of adults in Cullman County, with limits of 16.2% to 21.7%, and 16.0% in Madison County, with limits of 13.8% to 18.3%
. The same program puts adult depression at 26.5% in Cullman and 22.0% in Madison

short: Places to live with staff support for adults with mental illness. WellStone names supervised housing as a priority, and a court official put the wait for a group home at 100 days or more.
def: The Department of Mental Health funds residential services in grades that run from closely supervised homes to semi-independent apartments
. WellStone's plan lists residential facilities, including apartments and group homes, among its services
. The same plan names supervised housing for adult clients among its priorities for expansion
. The Madison County probate court's director of mental health programs said in May 2025 that the waiting list for group homes was at least 100 days

short: WellStone's prevention program, which has taught Mental Health First Aid to faculty and staff at the University of Alabama in Huntsville since 2023.
def: Heads Up Prevention is the WellStone program through which the University of Alabama in Huntsville has offered Mental Health First Aid training since the spring semester of 2023
. About 100 faculty and staff had completed the training by September 2026, in classes limited to 15 participants
. WellStone was also the Alabama Department of Mental Health's substance use prevention awardee for both the Madison and the Cullman catchment areas in fiscal year 2024

term: Health information exchange (Alabama One Health Record)
short: Alabama's network for sharing patient records electronically between hospitals, clinics and other providers. Certified clinics must connect their record systems to it.
def: A health information exchange lets one provider see what another has recorded, for instance that a patient was just discharged from hospital; Alabama One Health Record is the exchange set up by the Alabama Medicaid Agency

. The Alabama Department of Mental Health requires every Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic, WellStone included, to integrate its electronic health record, the system in which a provider keeps its patient records, with the exchange
. The exchange reported receiving 5,531,800 hospital discharge messages from 46 hospitals in calendar year 2025, and its governance includes a representative of Huntsville Hospital Health System
. Its briefing does not name which Madison or Cullman hospitals or mental health centers are connected

term: Health insurance marketplace (and its tax credits)
short: The federal exchange where people without job-based coverage buy insurance, often with a subsidy. About 95,000 Alabamians left it after enhanced tax credits expired at the end of 2025.
def: The Affordable Care Act set up marketplaces where individuals buy private plans and receive tax credits that lower the premium
. Enhanced credits expired at the end of 2025, and about 95,000 Alabamians, about 23% of the state's enrollees, left the marketplace

. In December 2025 the president of a hospital in the Huntsville Hospital system estimated that approximately 19,500 of the people expected to lose coverage were in the system's north Alabama territory
. The federal government publishes a county-level file of 2026 plan selections, and the Madison and Cullman rows could not be read for this report

short: The federal government's set of national health goals for the decade to 2030. This report uses its five-domain grouping of the social conditions that shape health.
def: Healthy People 2030 is the federal government's set of national health objectives, published by the federal Department of Health and Human Services

. It sorts the social determinants of health into five domains: economic stability, education access and quality, health care access and quality, neighborhood and built environment, and social and community context
. Housing falls in the neighborhood and built environment domain
. For that domain, the January 2025 count in the Huntsville continuum found 718 homeless people

short: A confidential 24-hour crisis counseling telephone line run by Crisis Services of North Alabama, separate from the 988 call center at WellStone.
def: The HELPline is a confidential, 24-hour crisis counseling line run by Crisis Services of North Alabama, whose other services include the HOPE Place emergency shelter for victims of domestic violence and support after sexual assault
. The same organization manages the 2-1-1 information line for Jackson, Limestone, Madison, Morgan, Marshall and DeKalb counties, a list that does not include Cullman
. Its home page gives no numbers of calls or people served

short: Madison County's not-for-profit ambulance service, which reports more than 65,000 calls a year. Its home page publishes nothing on behavioral health transports.
def: Huntsville Emergency Medical Services, Inc., known as HEMSI, describes itself as Madison County's not-for-profit emergency medical services provider, and reports 265 employees, 36 units and more than 65,000 calls a year
. Its home page publishes nothing on behavioral health transports and says nothing about peer support or wellness programs for its own staff
. WellStone's chief executive said in March 2024 that the service takes about 800 young people a year out of Madison County for psychiatric stabilization
. It was reported to have given naloxone about 380 times in the six months to early July 2024, a spoken estimate from the service

short: Programs that send a trained visitor to the homes of pregnant women and families with young children to support parenting and health.
def: Home visiting programs send a trained visitor to the homes of pregnant women and families with young children; Alabama's state program is First Teacher Home Visiting, run by the Department of Early Childhood Education
. In Huntsville the National Children's Advocacy Center runs home-visiting and parenting programs and reported 397 home visits to first-time parents in 2024
. The Department of Mental Health's autism resource guide also lists a First Teacher program run by UCP Huntsville

term: House Bill 70 of 2022 (the revised commitment law)
short: A 2022 Alabama law that added a ground for taking a person to a mental health facility and allowed courts to mandate outpatient care. It took effect in July 2022.
def: House Bill 70 added a condition under which a law enforcement officer can take a person to a mental health facility to be seen by a physician: that the person is unable to meet their medical and physical needs
. It also allowed courts to mandate outpatient care, and it took effect in July 2022
. Madison County's probate judge helped draft the bill, which a Huntsville representative sponsored
. The judge said in 2023 that with the law the court can convert inpatients to outpatients once they are stabilized and receiving treatment

short: The federal housing department's yearly list of the beds a homelessness continuum has, by type: emergency shelter, transitional housing, permanent supportive housing and rapid re-housing.
def: The housing inventory count is the federal housing department's yearly bed inventory for a continuum of care, with a summary table and a project-by-project list
. The 2025 inventory for the Huntsville continuum lists 684 year-round beds: 421 emergency shelter, 37 transitional housing, 190 permanent supportive housing and 36 rapid re-housing
. Permanent supportive housing stood at 334 beds in the 2022 inventory, 154 in 2023 and 153 in 2024
. The 2025 inventory for the Balance of State continuum, which contains Cullman County, shows 105 year-round beds in all

short: Housing assistance, also called Section 8, administered by local housing authorities. Cullman's waiting list is closed; Huntsville's authority assists close to 1,800 families.
def: Housing Choice Vouchers, also called Section 8 vouchers, are administered by local housing authorities
. The Cullman Housing Authority, whose voucher jurisdiction is Cullman County, says its waiting list is closed, opens only rarely and can mean a wait of months or years
. The Huntsville Housing Authority says it assists close to 1,800 families with vouchers
. In the 2022 federal housing inventory, 268 of the Huntsville continuum's 334 permanent supportive housing beds were in a Veterans Affairs voucher project

term: Huntsville Hospital Health System (Huntsville Hospital and Crestwood)
short: The hospital system owned by a public authority of the City of Huntsville. Since 31 March 2026 it has included Crestwood Medical Center as well as Huntsville Hospital.
def: Huntsville Hospital Health System is owned by a public authority, the Health Care Authority of the City of Huntsville
. On 31 March 2026 it completed its purchase of Crestwood Medical Center from the for-profit Community Health Systems
. Huntsville Hospital describes inpatient behavioral health care for adults and seniors and gives no bed count, and the hospital association's listing for Crestwood shows no psychiatric service
. The system's audit puts its uncompensated care at about $144.4 million for the year ended June 2025 and, as read, contains no figure for behavioral health revenue, cost or volume
. Huntsville Hospital is also a named partner in the federal grant for the probate court's assisted outpatient treatment program

short: The public housing agency for Huntsville, with more than 1,500 rental units and close to 1,800 voucher families. It holds most of the area's permanent supportive housing beds.
def: The Huntsville Housing Authority says it has over 1,500 rental units and assists close to 1,800 families with Section 8 vouchers
. It reports a wait of six to twelve months for public housing
. In the 2025 federal housing inventory its project accounts for 166 of the Huntsville continuum's 190 permanent supportive housing beds
. It received $615,231 for permanent supportive housing, the largest of the continuum's four federal grants for FY2024

term: Huntsville Transit (Orbit buses and Access paratransit)
short: The City of Huntsville's public transport: Orbit, the fixed-route bus, and Access, a booked service for riders who cannot use the standard bus.
def: Orbit, Huntsville's bus system, runs Monday to Friday from 6 a.m. to 9 p.m. and Saturday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with no Sunday service listed
. Access is the city's paratransit service, for people whose physical disabilities prevent use of the standard bus

. Paratransit has carried clients of the community mental health center since the 1990s and now provides up to 10,000 rides a year to and from WellStone's adult day treatment facility, with three Access operators assigned to that service
. WellStone requests each ride 24 hours in advance and clients receive a ticket for the trip
. The city's page for Orbit carries a 2022 modification date, so its hours may be out of date

short: The evidence-based model of supported employment for people with serious mental illness: help finding an ordinary paid job, then lasting support in it.
def: Supported employment places people in regular paid jobs and backs them up afterwards, and Individual Placement and Support is the tested model of it for people with serious mental illness
. Alabama's program is run by the Department of Mental Health with the Department of Rehabilitation Services
. In February 2025 the Department named five mental health centers that offer it, and none is in north Alabama

term: Infant and early childhood mental health
variants: infant and early childhood mental health
short: Support for the emotional development of children from birth to about five, delivered mainly through the adults who care for them.
def: Infant and early childhood mental health programs support the emotional development of children from birth to about five, working with parents, teachers and pediatricians as much as with the child
. The Department of Mental Health places consulting therapists in child-care and pediatric settings
. Its page names a state coordinator and links a provider search, and does not say how many consultants there are or which serve Madison or Cullman counties

short: A hospital unit where people are admitted for psychiatric care. Huntsville Hospital describes units for adults and seniors; Cullman County's hospital lists outpatient psychiatry only.
def: Huntsville Hospital describes inpatient care for the psychiatric needs of adults and seniors, entered through medical clearance and an assessment in its emergency department, and gives no bed count
. The hospital association's listing for Cullman Regional Medical Center shows outpatient psychiatric services only, and its listing for Crestwood shows no psychiatric service
. The Huntsville Hospital system's audit describes Decatur West as licensed for sixty-four psychiatric beds and gives no count of psychiatric beds at Huntsville Hospital itself
. A May 2025 television report said sixty mental health beds are in Madison County and serve patients from across north Alabama

term: Institution for mental disease (and Alabama's federal waiver)
short: Medicaid's term for a psychiatric facility of more than 16 beds, where it usually will not pay for adults aged 21 to 64. Alabama's waiver covers such stays only in Baldwin and Mobile counties.
def: An institution for mental disease is a hospital, nursing facility or other institution of more than 16 beds that mainly provides care for mental illness, and Medicaid has historically not paid for care in one for people aged 21 to 64
. A state can obtain a federal waiver of that rule; Alabama's, approved from 20 May 2022 to 19 May 2027, pays for stays of enrollees aged 21 to 64 only in institutions in Baldwin and Mobile counties
. Enrollees from any county may use those institutions, and no north Alabama facility is covered
. A separate Medicaid rule covers inpatient psychiatric services for recipients under 21

short: Secure custody for young people held by court order while they await a hearing. Madison County's center has 48 beds; Cullman County has a short-term facility of its own.
def: A juvenile detention center is a secure facility for young people detained by court order pending court hearings or acceptance into treatment programs
. The state's Department of Youth Services lists eleven in Alabama, among them Neaves-Davis in Huntsville with a capacity of 48
. Cullman County has a facility of its own, described by its juvenile probation chief in 2019 as short-term and renamed by the county commission in October 2024, which is not on the state's list
. Kids Count records 229 youth incarcerations in Madison County and 78 in Cullman County in 2014–2024, against 519 and 116 in 1999–2009

short: A collection of indicators of child well-being for Alabama and each county, compiled by VOICES for Alabama's Children.
def: Kids Count is a collection of indicators of child well-being for Alabama and each of its counties, compiled by VOICES for Alabama's Children from other sources; it is not a survey

. Its 2025 county profiles carry a small set of mental health rows: poor mental health days, the ratio of population to mental health providers, and the number of children with serious emotional disturbance receiving mental health services
. For 2024 they report 2,294 such children in Madison County and 444 in Cullman County
. The Cullman profile prints no source line for these indicators

short: A health service's duty to offer interpreters and other language help to people who speak little English. Alabama's clinic manual places it on WellStone.
def: Language access means offering language assistance, such as interpreters, to people with limited English proficiency; the national standards that cover it are known as CLAS, for Culturally and Linguistically Appropriate Services

. Alabama's manual for certified clinics requires interpretation or translation services that are readily available and appropriate to the size and needs of a clinic's population with limited English proficiency
. The requirement applies to WellStone as a certified clinic
. Hispanic or Latino residents are 7.6% of Madison County and 5.8% of Cullman County

short: The Huntsville organization for which this report was prepared, and the publisher of the statewide companion report.
def: Little Orange Fish is the Huntsville organization for which this report was prepared, and the publisher of the statewide Alabama Mental Health Systems Report
. The statewide report names it as the backbone organization for the North Alabama Mental Health Coalition
. The coalition's own list of core partners includes it

short: Personal experience of a mental or substance use disorder, one's own or a family member's. Alabama's clinic manual requires such people to have a part in governing a certified clinic.
def: In the rule this report discusses, the phrase covers people who have lived with a mental or substance use disorder and their families

. Alabama's manual for certified clinics requires that they take a meaningful part in a clinic's governance, through a governing board at least 51% made up of such people or through another arrangement
. A clinic that uses the alternative must support the posting of an annual summary of that body's recommendations on its website
. WellStone's board is appointed by four local governments
. It also has a Community Advisory Committee, on which the Madison County probate judge sits; no membership list, remit or count of consumer and family seats was found in the sources read

short: A shortage designation for the low-income people of an area: too few providers serve Medicaid and sliding-fee patients for the size of that population.
def: A low-income population designation is a shortage designation for the low-income population of a service area, and it shows a shortage of providers serving Medicaid and sliding-fee patients in comparison with that population
. Cullman County's designation is of this kind and covers the whole county
. In the federal file of 3 October 2026, ten counties of the ring carry the same kind of designation, with scores of 16 to 18 across the eleven counties
. The count behind a mental health designation includes psychiatrists only, so counselors, social workers, psychologists and nurse practitioners are left out

term: Madison County 310 Board and Cullman County 310 Authority
short: The two local boards that coordinate services for people with intellectual disabilities, one in each county. They are separate from WellStone, the 310 board for mental illness.
