def: Intellectual and developmental disabilities are lifelong conditions that begin in childhood; they are not mental illnesses, but in Alabama the same department is responsible for both
. The Madison County 310 Board, established by the City of Huntsville and the Madison County Commission in 1990, coordinates intellectual disability services in Madison County
. For Cullman County the plan on file is that of the Cullman County 310 Authority, also named as the Cullman County Center for the Developmentally Disabled
. Both report local government funding without stating the amounts

short: The range around a survey estimate within which the true value probably lies. For a small area such as a census tract it is often wide.
def: Each American Community Survey estimate on the regional map was taken with the margin of error the Census Bureau publishes for it
. Because the estimates are for small areas, many tract values have wide margins of error
. Two tracts whose ranges overlap should not be ranked against each other on that estimate alone.

short: The public health insurance program for low-income people, paid for jointly by the federal government and the state and run in Alabama by the Alabama Medicaid Agency.
def: Medicaid is public health insurance for low-income people, run by each state within federal rules; in Alabama the Alabama Medicaid Agency, a separate agency from the Department of Mental Health, decides who is eligible, what is covered and what providers are paid
. The agency counted 54,803 eligible people in Madison County and 15,922 in Cullman County in April 2026
. It reports that 18% of Madison County's population was eligible at some point in fiscal year 2024, one of the five lowest county shares in the state
. Its rule requires a provider of rehabilitative mental health services to be certified as a 310-board community mental health center, and the center for these two counties is WellStone

short: Alabama Medicaid's count of people eligible for the program. A monthly count and the share eligible at any point in a year are different measures and give different percentages.
def: Alabama Medicaid publishes a monthly count of eligibles for each county: 54,803 in Madison County and 15,922 in Cullman County in April 2026, both lower than a year earlier
. The table as read carries no footnote defining "eligibles" or saying whether children in ALL Kids are included
. A different measure is the share of a county's population eligible at some point during a year, which the agency put at 18% for Madison County in fiscal year 2024
. Census survey estimates for 2024 put Medicaid coverage at 9.77% of Madison County residents and 15.9% of Cullman County residents

short: The Medicaid benefit that pays for community mental health treatment. A mental health provider must be a center certified by the Department of Mental Health, which in these two counties is WellStone.
def: Alabama Medicaid covers community mental health and substance use treatment under a benefit called rehabilitative services

. Under the agency's rule a mental health provider must be certified by the Department of Mental Health as a 310-board community mental health center, and payment is a statewide maximum for each procedure code
. For Madison and Cullman counties that center is WellStone, which states that it is certified by the Department

short: Treating opioid addiction with a prescribed medicine, such as buprenorphine or methadone, usually alongside counseling.
def: Medication-assisted treatment means treating opioid addiction with a prescribed medicine, such as buprenorphine or methadone, usually alongside counseling; the medicines reduce craving and withdrawal and lower the risk of overdose
. Bradford Health Services' Madison campus lists it among its services
. WellStone's 2022 federal grant was announced as supporting medication-assisted treatment "to counter the ongoing overdose crisis"
. Opioid treatment clinics in Huntsville and in Cullman dispense both methadone and buprenorphine

term: Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama
variants: Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama
short: The community mental health center for Lawrence, Limestone and Morgan counties, based in Decatur. One of the four centers that serve the ring.
def: The Mental Health Center of North Central Alabama is a public nonprofit that has served Lawrence, Limestone and Morgan counties since 1967, with sites in Decatur, Athens and Moulton
. It says it treated over 3,525 children and adults in 2023 with about 140 staff; the Department of Mental Health's FY2025 report counts 2,694 people served
. It broke ground on 10 December 2024 on a 16-bed crisis residential unit in Decatur for people committed to the Department, with completion expected by October 2025
. On 4 October 2026 it was advertising for nurses for the unit, and no source confirmed that it had opened

short: An eight-hour course that teaches members of the public to recognize and respond to someone developing a mental health problem or in crisis.
def: Mental Health First Aid is an eight-hour course that teaches people who are not clinicians to recognize and respond to someone developing a mental health problem or in crisis
. WellStone's Heads Up program has delivered it at the University of Alabama in Huntsville since spring 2023, and about 100 faculty and staff had completed it by September 2026
. NAMI Madison County Alabama also lists the course among its programs

short: A place, population or facility the federal government has designated as short of mental health providers. Cullman County has one; Madison County has no area designation.
def: A Health Professional Shortage Area, or HPSA, is a designation by the federal health workforce agency that a geographic area, a population within an area, or a facility has too few providers
. For mental health the designation counts psychiatrists only, and the threshold is a population of at least 30,000 for each psychiatrist, or 20,000 where needs are unusually high
. Cullman County is designated as a whole county for its low-income population, with a score of 16
. Madison County has no current area designation and is the only Alabama county without one
. A designation is a gateway to federal help such as loan repayment for clinicians who work there

short: A school-district employee who links students and families to mental health services but does not provide treatment. State law requires every district to have one.
def: A coordinator connects students and families to services and does not provide treatment; a 2022 state law required every school district to employ one
. Madison County Schools names a mental health services coordinator and describes a three-tiered model of support with school social workers and counselors
. Cullman County Schools had a coordinator and four full-time social workers in February 2022
. Cullman City Schools employs a district mental health specialist who works across kindergarten to grade 12

short: Two medicines prescribed to treat opioid addiction. They reduce craving and withdrawal and lower the risk of overdose.
def: Methadone and buprenorphine are medicines prescribed to treat opioid addiction; they reduce craving and withdrawal and lower the risk of overdose
. Methadone is dispensed through certified opioid treatment programs, some of which also offer buprenorphine and naltrexone
. The clinic in Cullman lists methadone, buprenorphine, extended-release buprenorphine injections and naltrexone
. On weekdays the two Huntsville clinics dispense from 5:00 a.m., one until 11:45 a.m. and the other until 11:00 a.m., so a dose has to be collected in the morning

short: Clinicians who travel to a person in crisis, at home or elsewhere in the community. WellStone runs adult and child teams in both Madison and Cullman counties.
def: A mobile crisis team is the "someone to respond" of the crisis model: clinicians who travel to the person in crisis
. Cullman County's adult team was announced in June 2020 as a state-funded pilot with a two-person team on every shift, around the clock
. WellStone's plan says it runs mobile crisis teams for adults and for children in both counties
. Its child and adolescent teams served 498 young people in fiscal year 2025, of 936 served by all such teams in Alabama

short: A van WellStone announced in November 2025, to offer therapy and dispense psychiatric medication, starting at First Stop and the Downtown Rescue Mission.
def: In November 2025 WellStone announced a van that it called the state's first mobile mental health clinic, saying it would be deployed in the coming weeks
. The vehicle is a place for therapy sessions and also a mobile dispensing unit for psychiatric medications

. It was to begin through partnerships with First Stop and the Downtown Rescue Mission in Madison County, and was paid for by a grant from Huntsville Hospital's Community Health Initiative with other donations
. The announcement forecast that it would help thousands of Madison County residents past transportation, scheduling and other barriers

short: The community mental health center for Jackson and Marshall counties, in the ring. It became the ring's first Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic in October 2025.
def: Mountain Lakes Behavioral Healthcare is the community mental health center that the Department of Mental Health assigns to Jackson and Marshall counties, two of the thirteen ring counties

. It received federal approval to move to the Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic model in October 2025, the only one of the four ring centers to have done so by the time of the Department's announcement in May 2026
. The Department's directory lists its full-scope clinic sites in Guntersville and Scottsboro
. The Department counts 3,129 people served by it in fiscal year 2025

short: A medicine that reverses an opioid overdose within minutes, often given as a nasal spray.
def: Naloxone is a medicine that reverses an opioid overdose within minutes and can be given by a bystander, which is why states distribute it widely
. The state opioid council's 2025 report lists Madison County, with 2,344 doses between 1 November 2024 and 31 October 2025, among the counties with the highest distribution
. Cullman County is not mentioned anywhere in the text of that report
. Huntsville's ambulance service was reported to have given the drug about 380 times in the six months to early July 2024

short: The state organization of the National Alliance on Mental Illness and its local affiliate. Madison County has an affiliate; none is listed for Cullman County.
def: NAMI Alabama is the state organization of the National Alliance on Mental Illness, a membership group of people with mental illness and their families
. It lists eleven local affiliates; NAMI Madison County is one, and none is listed for Cullman County
. NAMI Madison County runs a family support group, Connection peer groups and an eight-week class for families
. NAMI Alabama also runs the crisis intervention training program for police, with the Huntsville Police Department as the hub for its eighteen-county Region 1

short: The local affiliate of the National Alliance on Mental Illness. It runs peer and family support groups and a course for families. No affiliate is listed for Cullman County.
def: NAMI Madison County Alabama is one of the affiliates of NAMI Alabama, the state organization of the National Alliance on Mental Illness
. It describes itself as an organization of families, friends and individuals whose lives have been affected by mental illness

. It runs a family support group for Huntsville and Madison, Connection groups for people with mental health conditions, one of which meets in Athens in Limestone County, and an eight-week course for families
. NAMI Alabama lists eleven affiliates and none in Cullman County

short: A Huntsville center, opened in 1985, that brings prosecutors, police, child welfare staff and therapists together on child abuse cases and offers trauma therapy to children.
def: The National Children's Advocacy Center opened in Huntsville on 1 May 1985

. It runs a multidisciplinary team for child abuse cases, drawn from the district attorney's office, law enforcement, the Department of Human Resources, forensic interviewers, family advocates, therapists and medical professionals
. It offers trauma therapy to children up to 18 and says no child is denied services because of a family's finances

short: Madison County's 48-bed juvenile detention center in Huntsville, which holds young people detained by court order.
def: The Neaves-Davis Center for Children is Madison County's juvenile detention facility, with 48 beds, licensed to the standards of the Alabama Department of Youth Services
. It holds juveniles detained by court order while they await hearings or acceptance into treatment programs
. Juveniles detained in Huntsville are held there
. The county's page says nothing about medical, education or mental health services for the young people held

term: North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless (the Huntsville continuum)
variants: North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless
short: The homelessness continuum of care for Madison, Limestone and Morgan counties. Federal counts and housing inventories for the Huntsville continuum cover all three.
def: The North Alabama Coalition for the Homeless is the continuum of care, numbered AL-503, for Madison, Limestone and Morgan counties
. It describes its work as connecting people to housing, healthcare and supportive services, with a focus on people experiencing substance use and mental health challenges
. The City of Huntsville says its Community Development department leads the partner agencies working through the continuum and partners with the coalition on the annual count
. Federal continuum funding for FY2024 was $945,663 in four grants, the largest of them $615,231 to the Huntsville Housing Authority for permanent supportive housing

short: A Huntsville-area coalition of mental health stakeholders, formed in 2015 by a committee of the Society of St. Vincent de Paul.
def: The coalition was formed in 2015 by the Voice of the Poor Committee of the Society of St. Vincent de Paul in Huntsville, to improve the situation of people with serious mental illness, many of them homeless or in jail
. It describes itself as community mental health stakeholders who share knowledge and resources to find and address gaps in access to care
. Its listed core partners include WellStone, Huntsville Hospital, the sheriff's department, the Huntsville and Madison police, First Stop, the probate judges and Little Orange Fish
. In 2018 it asked the Huntsville City Council and the Madison County Commission to help fund WellStone's jail diversion program
. The statewide report names Little Orange Fish as its backbone organization, so where this report describes the coalition it is describing a body that the organization it was prepared for belongs to

short: The state psychiatric hospital in Decatur, with 74 beds, whose closure the state announced in January 2015.
def: North Alabama Regional Hospital was a state hospital in Decatur with a bed capacity of 74
. On 13 January 2015 officials of the Department of Mental Health announced a plan to close it by 30 June of that year

. The commissioner said its patients would be served by acute care units at hospitals, crisis stabilization units, intermediate care facilities run by community mental health centers, or Bryce Hospital if necessary

short: The community mental health center for Fayette, Lamar, Marion, Walker and Winston counties. It runs its own mobile crisis service and crisis residential beds.
def: Northwest Alabama Mental Health Center is the center the Department of Mental Health assigns to Fayette, Lamar, Marion, Walker and Winston counties
. It runs mobile crisis in two of them, Marion and Winston, and a 16-bed crisis residential unit for adults at Townley in Walker County that takes referrals statewide
. Under a management contract dating from 2001 it also runs a 24-bed behavioral medicine unit at the hospital in Jasper
. Its plan reports 10,317 consumers in 2023, a figure that includes substance use and disability services, against 3,306 people served in the Department's FY2025 report

short: WellStone's service for children and adolescents in Huntsville, offering individual, group and family counseling. A similar name, NOVA-Huntsville, belongs to its psychosis program.
def: The Nova Center for Youth & Family is the part of WellStone through which children and adolescents receive individual, group and family counseling, as WellStone's strategic plan describes it
. WellStone's website names it as one of eight service locations
. The Alabama Department of Mental Health's directories also list it as a substance use treatment provider, at 1900 Golf Road SW in Huntsville
. A similar name, NOVA-Huntsville, belongs to the first-episode psychosis program that WellStone runs as one of three such sites in Alabama

short: Short-stay beds in a crisis center where a person is watched and treated for hours or a few days without being admitted to a hospital.
def: Observation beds are short-stay beds in a crisis center; a stay is voluntary and brief, and its aim is to settle the crisis and arrange what comes next
. WellStone Emergency Services was built with a temporary observation unit of up to 15 beds, for stays of 24 hours or less, and an extended observation unit of up to 24 beds that started with 16
. The maximum for the two units together is 39
. The temporary center that preceded it had ten beds on its inpatient side and ten on its temporary observation side

term: Office of Alternative Sentencing and Release (Madison County)
variants: Office of Alternative Sentencing and Release
short: The Madison County department that runs pretrial release, community corrections, misdemeanor probation, court referral and the adult drug court for the county's courts.
def: A Madison County department that provides the circuit and district courts with alternative sanctions
. Pretrial release, community corrections, misdemeanor probation, court referral and the adult drug court all sit in it
. Its Mental Health Pre-Trial Release Program interviews, evaluates and supervises jail detainees who show signs of mental illness or have a diagnosis
. The general pretrial release program evaluates detainees who apply for release on personal recognizance or an unsecured bond and monitors those released
. The department's page publishes no caseload numbers

short: The list of things this report could not read, confirm or find, each with where it was looked for and what would settle it.
def: The open items are the report's record of what it could not settle: documents that would not open, figures that need a person to read them by eye, announcements whose outcome could not be confirmed, and counts that were looked for and not found. Appendix C prints the principal ones and the Open Items page lists them all, with where each was looked for. An open item says the thing was not found in the sources read; it does not say the thing does not exist.

short: Money paid under legal settlements with companies that made and distributed opioids. The state, the counties and the cities each receive a share and decide how to spend it.
def: States sued companies that made and distributed opioid painkillers, and the settlements pay out over a number of years
. Huntsville's first allocations, announced in April 2023, were $850,000 to the Huntsville Hospital Foundation, $810,000 to First Stop and $750,000 to WellStone
. Madison County is using settlement funds to pay for an additional mental health nurse in its jail
. Cullman County gave a one-time $250,000 to the Good Samaritan Health Clinic and approved $150,000 over three years for the district attorney's drug court

. At state level the Department of Mental Health gave WellStone $660,000 of a $3,000,000 appropriation for 988 call centers, and says the River Crossing detox beds are funded by a grant from the state fund

short: A clinic certified to dispense methadone, and often buprenorphine, for opioid use disorder. Huntsville has two and Cullman one.
def: An opioid treatment program is a certified clinic that dispenses methadone for opioid use disorder; some also offer buprenorphine and naltrexone
. The Alabama Department of Mental Health says Alabama has 21 of them, in 16 counties that include Madison and Cullman
. In Huntsville, BHG Huntsville Treatment Center and New Season's Huntsville Metro Treatment Center both dispense methadone and buprenorphine and accept Medicaid and Medicare
. In Cullman, BHG Cullman Treatment Center is at 1912 Commerce Avenue NW, the street on which WellStone's campus also stands

short: The one drop-in center for people with mental illness that the Department of Mental Health lists in north Alabama, on Max Luther Drive in Huntsville.
def: Our Place, at 205 Max Luther Drive in Huntsville, is the only drop-in center in north Alabama among the five the Alabama Department of Mental Health lists for people with mental illness
. The Department describes drop-in centers as free and voluntary community spaces, some standalone and some run through local mental health providers
. It lists none in Cullman County

term: PATHS (the state's telephone consultation service for pediatricians)
short: A statewide line through which children's doctors can consult child mental health specialists at Children's of Alabama. Families do not call it directly.
def: PATHS, Pediatric Access to Telemental Health Services, is a consultation line through which primary care practices get advice from child mental health specialists at Children's of Alabama on diagnosing and managing mild to moderate conditions
. It is a service for clinicians, and families do not call it directly
. In a 2024 article on the program, Children's of Alabama said it can take three to six months to see a therapist or psychiatrist
. The article gives no enrollment counts or psychiatrist numbers

term: Pediatric crisis unit (WellStone Pediatric Crisis Care)
short: WellStone's 24-bed crisis unit for young people in Huntsville, opened in late September 2024 and listed by the state with the adult crisis center.
def: WellStone's pediatric crisis unit opened in late September 2024 with 24 beds for ages 12 to 18, and cost $9 million
. A television report of its unveiling was headlined as the first of its kind in the state
. A month after it opened, a staffing shortage meant it could treat six patients at a time

. For its first year there are two counts: the Department of Mental Health's 520 served in fiscal year 2025, and WellStone's statement that it had served 400 individuals and had begun taking patients as young as eight
. The Department lists it together with the adult center, at one address and with one list of fifteen counties

short: A walk-in space where peers offer support. WellStone's 2022 federal grant promised one serving 400 people; no source says whether it opened.
def: In the abstract of its 2022 federal grant WellStone committed to expand peer services "with a living room model" and to give walk-in support to 400 people through a Peer Support Living Room
. The grant's project period ran from 30 September 2022 to 29 September 2026
. The federal award record carries the figure as one of the numeric goals in the project abstract

short: A community center for people seeking recovery from addiction, staffed by peers who are in recovery themselves. The state lists one in Huntsville and none in Cullman County.
def: A recovery community center staffed by peers
. The Department of Mental Health's directory lists one in Huntsville, the Madison County Community Center run by R.O.S.S., open from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. every day, and none in Cullman County
. R.O.S.S., the Recovery Organization of Support Specialists, describes its peer support specialists as people living in recovery from a substance use disorder
. The Partnership for a Drug-Free Community also runs a recovery hub in Huntsville that it says is staffed by state-certified peer recovery support specialists

short: Long-term housing paired with support services, aimed at people leaving homelessness. In the Huntsville continuum it went from 334 beds in 2022 to 190 in 2025.
def: Supportive housing pairs an ordinary home with visiting support services so that a person with serious mental illness can live in the community; housing agencies say "permanent supportive housing" when it is aimed at people leaving homelessness
. The federal housing inventory for the Huntsville continuum shows 334 year-round permanent supportive housing beds in 2022, 154 in 2023, 153 in 2024 and 190 in 2025
. The 2025 inventory lists two projects: a Huntsville Housing Authority project with 166 beds and WellStone's Shelter Plus Care with 24
. That continuum covers Madison, Limestone and Morgan counties and does not include Cullman

short: A count of everyone found homeless, in shelters and outdoors, on a single night in January. Each homelessness continuum conducts one and the federal housing department publishes it.
def: The point-in-time count is a count of everyone found homeless, in shelters and on the street, on a single night in January, which federal rules require each continuum of care to conduct
. It is a snapshot that depends on weather and on how many volunteers search, and it is better for rough scale than for year-to-year change
. The federal report of the count of 28 January 2025 for the Huntsville continuum gives 718 people: 416 in emergency shelter, 37 in transitional housing and 265 unsheltered
. The number listed as severely mentally ill has moved erratically, from 71 in 2022 to 24 in 2023, 40 in 2024 and 49 in 2025

short: A County Health Rankings measure given as a number of days a month: 5.4 in Madison County and 5.7 in Cullman County in the March 2026 figures.
def: Poor mental health days is a measure that County Health Rankings gives as a number of days a month; its March 2026 figures are 5.4 for Madison County and 5.7 for Cullman County
. The Kids Count county profiles print values for 2022, 5.5 in Madison County and 6.2 in Cullman County

short: The county court that hears petitions for involuntary commitment in Alabama. Madison County's also runs an outpatient commitment program with WellStone.
def: Probate courts are county courts best known for wills and estates; in Alabama they also hear petitions for civil commitment, and the probate judge holds the hearing and issues the order

. Madison County's probate court announced an assisted outpatient treatment program with WellStone, to start on 3 February 2020 and paid for at first from the passport application fees the court collects
. Cullman County's probate court lists commitments among its case types, and its web page publishes no procedure, forms or counts
. The yearly figures quoted for Madison County, such as 414 petitions in 2021 and a peak of 589 involuntary commitments in 2023, come from press reports

short: Probation is supervision in the community in place of prison; parole is supervised release after part of a prison sentence. Both carry conditions and can be revoked.
def: Probation is supervision in the community in place of prison, and parole is supervised release after part of a prison sentence has been served; both put a person under conditions and an officer's supervision, and both can be revoked
. In Madison County a county office supervises people on probation for the District Court in misdemeanor cases and in certain felony cases
. The state's day reporting center in Huntsville is for high-risk probationers and parolees
. The Madison County office's page publishes no caseload numbers

short: A suicide prevention initiative that Cullman Regional Medical Center says it has joined. No results have been reported.
def: Cullman Regional's 2025 implementation plan says the hospital "has recently partnered with Project Zero Suicide"

. Implementing it is one of the hospital's mental health strategies, with continued support for partner organizations, outpatient psychiatry and a behavioral health treatment area in the emergency room
. The hospital's board adopted the plan on 11 March 2025
. No result of the partnership was found in the sources read

term: Provider ratio (residents per mental health provider)
short: The number of residents for each mental health provider of any kind. Published figures for Madison and Cullman differ by source and by who is counted.
def: A provider ratio divides population by mental health providers of all kinds, not psychiatrists alone; it counts licensed people, not hours worked, and does not show whether they take Medicaid
. County Health Rankings' March 2026 figures give 474 residents per provider in Madison County and 568 in Cullman County, against 639 for Alabama
. The Kids Count county profiles print 500 and 609 for 2024
. Cullman Regional's needs assessment turns the fraction over and reports 132.0 providers per 100,000 residents in Cullman County in 2024, against 140.9 for Alabama and 312.5 for the United States
. County Health Rankings warns that some providers on the registry behind its count may no longer be practicing or accepting new patients, which may overstate supply in some communities

short: An advanced practice nurse specializing in mental health care. The University of Alabama in Huntsville offers a training track requiring 720 clinical hours.
def: A psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner is an advanced practice nurse specializing in mental health care, one of the provider types County Health Rankings counts in its provider ratio

. The College of Nursing at the University of Alabama in Huntsville offers a hybrid track that requires 720 clinical hours, at least 600 of them in direct patient care, and 1,000 hours of experience as a registered nurse before clinical work begins
. The program page gives no cohort size, launch date or count of graduates
. Federal mental health shortage designations measure psychiatrists only, so nurse practitioners do not figure in them

short: The years of supervised training a doctor completes after medical school to become a psychiatrist. A four-year program in Huntsville takes up to six residents a year.
def: A psychiatry residency is the supervised hospital training a doctor completes after medical school to become a psychiatrist, and because doctors tend to settle near where they train, residency places are a main lever on the supply of psychiatrists
. The University of Alabama at Birmingham runs a four-year program at its Huntsville Regional Medical Campus that accepts up to six residents a year
. The American Medical Association's residency database names Huntsville Hospital as the program's participating site
. The program's page listed six first-year and six second-year residents in October 2026 and none more senior
. The same database carries a separate four-year psychiatry program under WellStone's name, with six first-year positions and applications open

short: A peer-run organization supporting recovery from substance use. The Department of Mental Health lists Huntsville among its locations and none in Cullman.
def: The Recovery Organization of Support Specialists, known as ROSS, is a peer-run organization for recovery from substance use, which means it is led and staffed by people who have themselves lived with addiction
. The Alabama Department of Mental Health lists Huntsville as one of its six locations, gives a telephone line open from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m. daily, and shows no Cullman location
. On Save a Life Day 2025 its Madison County branch distributed 1,278 doses of naloxone

short: The return of a person from prison or jail to the community, and the services that support it. It is Intercept 4 of the Sequential Intercept Model.
def: Reentry is the return of a person from prison or jail to the community, and Intercept 4 of the Sequential Intercept Model
. For people with mental illness the risks at release are losing medication, coverage and housing at once
. In Madison County, WellStone's jail diversion staff work to get people held because of mental health problems out of jail, into stable housing and to their follow-up appointments
. In Cullman County, The Link received a federal grant in 2020 for a reentry program of case management and follow-up

short: A label with three different meanings in north Alabama: a mental illness services region, a 13-county Community Services office region and an 18-county police training region.
def: The Department of Mental Health's mental illness services map draws a Region 1 that the statewide edition read as twenty counties and seven centers; the membership is printed only in the map image and could not be read again for this report

. The Department's Regional Offices page lists a Region I Community Services office in Decatur covering thirteen counties, which include Madison and Cullman and leave Fayette, Lamar, Marion, Walker and Winston to a Region II office in Tuscaloosa
. NAMI Alabama's crisis intervention training program has its own Region 1 of eighteen north Alabama counties, with the Huntsville Police Department as its training hub

term: SAMHSA (Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration)
short: The federal agency for mental health and addiction services, part of the Department of Health and Human Services. It made three grants to WellStone between fiscal years 2021 and 2025.
def: SAMHSA is the federal agency for mental health and addiction services and is part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
. The federal department's grants database shows three SAMHSA awards to WellStone between fiscal years 2021 and 2025, totaling $9,575,938

. They are a community mental health center grant, later reduced to $2,502,021; $3,974,261 in four installments to implement the Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic model; and $3,099,656 for assisted outpatient treatment
. The project periods of the last two ended on 29 September 2026 and 30 July 2026

term: School-based mental health services (School-Based Mental Health Collaboration)
short: Therapy and other mental health care delivered on school grounds. In Madison County the providers include WellStone and a nonprofit, The Enrichment Center.
def: The School-Based Mental Health Collaboration is a joint program of the Department of Mental Health and the State Department of Education that places community mental health center clinicians in schools
. The Department says 122 school systems and 19 centers take part; its list of which systems partner with which center returned an error on 4 October 2026
. WellStone's Cullman site is listed as part of the collaboration

. In Madison City Schools the therapists on school grounds come from The Enrichment Center, a Huntsville nonprofit that reports 35 school-based therapists, 1,290 students and 14,166 therapy sessions in 2025–26 and does not bill insurance
. WellStone's therapists were reported to have served Madison County students more than 1,700 times in fiscal year 2024

short: A federal grant source for programs that help people returning from jail or prison. A $500,000 grant went to The Link of Cullman County in 2020.
def: The federal Second Chance Act is the source of a $500,000 grant that The Link of Cullman County received in 2020 for an adult reentry program
. The program was to provide case management, cognitive intervention and follow-up to a minimum of 40 medium- to high-risk people a year
. Named ONE-Eighty, it was due to begin enrolling in October 2020, with the Cullman County Sheriff's Office as a partner and referrals from the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles
. Both press reports date from 2020, the second from shortly before enrollment was due to begin

short: A map of the six points, numbered 0 to 5, at which a person with mental illness can be turned from the criminal justice system toward treatment.
def: The model lays the justice system out as a path and marks six points on it, numbered 0 to 5: community services, law enforcement, initial detention and first court hearings, jails and courts, reentry, and community corrections
. Communities use it to find gaps and opportunities at each point, and the earlier the intercept, the less time a person spends in the justice system
. In this region Intercept 0 includes the Huntsville crisis center, to which law enforcement and first responders in fifteen counties can bring a person in crisis at any hour
. As WellStone described it in April 2024, a Cullman County caller to 988 is connected to the Huntsville center, which connects them to a local crisis team

short: The children's counterpart of serious mental illness: a diagnosable disorder in someone under 18 that seriously limits life at home, at school or with others.
def: Serious emotional disturbance is the term federal programs use for children where they use serious mental illness for adults: a diagnosable disorder in someone under 18 that seriously limits life at home, at school or with others
. Kids Count reports that 2,294 Madison County children and 444 Cullman County children with serious emotional disturbance received mental health services in 2024
. The Cullman profile prints no source line for the figure

short: The public record draws WellStone's service area three ways: two counties for routine care, fifteen for the crisis center, and a Region 1 that has three meanings of its own.
def: The first map is two counties: the Department of Mental Health's county list assigns Madison and Cullman, and only those, to WellStone as their community mental health center
. The second is fifteen: the Department's Crisis Centers page lists fifteen counties as served by WellStone's crisis center in Huntsville

. The third is Region 1, a name used for a region on the Department's mental illness services map, for a thirteen-county Community Services office region, and for NAMI Alabama's eighteen-county police training region
. Other regional schemes cut across all three: the fifteen counties are split among three public health districts, four homelessness continuums and six area agencies on aging

short: WellStone's permanent supportive housing project, with 24 beds in the 2025 federal housing inventory for the Huntsville continuum.
def: Shelter Plus Care is the name under which WellStone's housing project appears in the federal housing inventory for the Huntsville continuum
. The 2025 inventory lists it with 24 beds, one of only two permanent supportive housing projects; the other is a Huntsville Housing Authority project with 166
. The 24 beds are part of the continuum's total of 190

short: A number attached to each federal shortage designation. Federal loan repayment for clinicians is tied to the score of the site where they work.
def: Each federal shortage designation carries a score, and the one for Cullman County's whole-county designation is 16
. National Health Service Corps loan repayment is tied to the score, with awards ranging from $30,000 to $75,000 for two years of full-time service
. In the federal file of 3 October 2026 the designated counties of the Huntsville crisis center's catchment have scores of 16 to 18

short: A charge that falls with a patient's income, so that people with low incomes pay little or nothing.
def: A sliding fee scale sets a charge according to income, which results in low-cost or free services for people with low incomes; the Alabama Department of Mental Health says every state-funded substance use provider charges this way
. The federal low-income shortage designation turns on how many providers serve Medicaid and sliding-fee patients
. Alabama's manual for Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics treats the sliding scale fee discount schedule as a document vital to a person's access to services
. WellStone states that no one is turned away for inability to pay; its own fee schedule was not found in any source that could be opened

short: The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, the federal food benefit once called food stamps.
def: SNAP is the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, a federally funded food benefit administered in Alabama by the Department of Human Resources
. In 2023, 34,783 people in Madison County and 8,554 in Cullman County received it
. The Link of Cullman County's director said in October 2025 that over $1 million in SNAP benefits is distributed in the county each month

short: A camp for unsheltered people in Huntsville that the city manages. It was rebuilt after a 2024 fire with marked spaces and a perimeter fence.
def: The South Derrick Street Camp is a camp for unsheltered people managed by the City of Huntsville's Community Development department with providers from the homelessness continuum
. After a 2024 fire the city rebuilt it with an asphalt pad, 84 individual spaces with tents on platforms and a perimeter fence, and required occupants to register and sign community standards
. Press reports in 2026 gave its capacity as about 58 people, with around 30 to 35 staying there
. People staying there must take part in case management, and the city said in June 2026 that its Homeless Services Team had helped 22 former residents into stable housing in six months

term: Specialty courts (mental health, veterans and drug courts)
short: Court dockets that put eligible defendants under supervised treatment in place of ordinary prosecution or jail. Both counties have set up mental health, veterans and drug court dockets.
def: A specialty court is a docket within an ordinary court in which a judge supervises a defendant through treatment and regular hearings, and completing the program can reduce or avoid a sentence

. Cullman County's veterans treatment court held its first session on 30 May 2019, and its mental health court for nonviolent offenders began in late May 2022 with WellStone as a partner, alongside an existing drug court
. Participants in the Cullman mental health court must plead guilty first and can have their charges dismissed by meeting milestones the court sets

. In Madison County the circuit's website says a district judge has presided over the Adult Mental Health Court since 2015 and that a circuit judge established a veterans court, and Huntsville's Municipal Court runs a mental health court of its own
. Madison County's adult drug court is run from the county's Office of Alternative Sentencing and Release

term: State evaluation office (Alabama Commission on the Evaluation of Services)
short: The state commission that evaluates whether state programs work. Its September 2025 report on the crisis centers found their monthly reporting inconsistent.
def: The Alabama Commission on the Evaluation of Services is a state commission, created in 2019, that evaluates state programs and advises the Legislature and the Governor

. Its preliminary evaluation of the Department of Mental Health's six crisis centers, published in September 2025, found the centers' monthly data reports inconsistent and said a consistent method was needed to judge their effectiveness

. For WellStone alone it gives only the split of spending: capital was 74.5% of the crisis center's expenditure in fiscal year 2021 and 78.6% in 2022, and by 2024 operations and administration were 87.3%
. It reported that crisis centers may serve fewer people from communities outside the metropolitan areas where they are located

term: State Health Plan (psychiatric bed need rule)
short: Alabama's planning rule for inpatient psychiatric beds. It decides by region when more beds may be added; Madison and Cullman fall in a ten-county North Region.
def: The State Health Plan's rule on psychiatric care, effective 14 June 2024, uses a regional method to judge the need for inpatient psychiatric beds, with three bed categories: child and adolescent, adult and geriatric
. It places Madison, Morgan and Cullman counties in a ten-county North Region
. A region becomes eligible for more beds when its occupancy is 75 percent or greater
. The rule prints no inventory of psychiatric beds by facility or region and refers readers to the planning agency's Data Division

short: A psychiatric hospital owned and run by the state. North Alabama's, in Decatur, closed in 2015, which left the state's remaining hospitals in Tuscaloosa.
def: A state hospital is a psychiatric hospital owned and run by the state, and Alabama's are operated by the Department of Mental Health
. The one that served north Alabama, North Alabama Regional Hospital in Decatur, had a bed capacity of 74 when officials announced on 13 January 2015 a plan to close it by 30 June
. Officials called it the third closure of a state hospital since 2012
. The Department's annual report for the period says the closure left all remaining state hospitals in Tuscaloosa

short: A national initiative to reduce the number of people with mental illness in county jails. Madison and Cullman counties were both first-year Alabama sites in 2018–19.
def: Stepping Up is a national initiative to reduce the number of people with mental illness in county jails; counties that join commit to steps such as screening everyone booked into jail, and in Alabama the Department of Mental Health administers it
. WellStone ran two of the six first-year Alabama sites, in Madison and Cullman counties, from October 2018 to September 2019
. That year Madison's site screened 82 jail inmates, of whom 35 screened positive; in Cullman four of the 98 inmates the jail referred agreed to be screened
. Both were sites again in 2020–21, when the state's report recorded 63 jail referrals in Madison and 11 in Cullman and said Madison's data were inconsistent

short: Deaths by suicide per 100,000 residents, averaged over several years. County Health Rankings gives 15.3 for Madison County and 20.7 for Cullman County.
def: A rate divides a count by population so that places of different size can be compared, and suicide rates are stated per 100,000 residents
. County Health Rankings' March 2026 supplement gives age-adjusted rates for 2019 to 2023 of 15.3 per 100,000 in Madison County and 20.7 in Cullman County
. Cullman Regional's 2025 assessment gives 20.6 per 100,000 for Cullman County as a 2018 to 2022 average, against 16.5 for Alabama and 14.5 nationally
. Among the ring counties the County Health Rankings values run from 13.8 in Limestone to 24.4 in Fayette, and Lamar's is suppressed

short: A federal payment for disabled people with very low income, run by the Social Security Administration. It is separate from the disability insurance earned through past work.
def: Supplemental Security Income is a federal payment, run by the Social Security Administration, that depends on need; Social Security Disability Insurance is the separate benefit that depends on a person's work record
. For many adults with serious mental illness one of the two is the main income
. In December 2024, 6,140 Madison County residents received SSI, 5,726 of them on grounds of blindness or disability, and 2,241 Cullman County residents, 2,107 of them on those grounds

term: System of care (children's mental health framework)
short: A national framework holding that services for children with serious mental health needs should be family-driven, community-based and coordinated across agencies.
def: The system of care approach dates from the 1980s and holds that services for children with serious emotional difficulties should be organized as a coordinated network that works in partnership with families and young people
. Its core values are care that is family driven and youth guided, community based, and fitted to a family's culture and language

. Among the pieces of such a network in this region, the Department of Mental Health lists case management, outpatient care, a juvenile court liaison, an in-home intervention program and the school-based collaboration for children at WellStone's Cullman site

term: Taylor Hardin Secure Medical Facility (the state's forensic hospital)
short: Alabama's forensic psychiatric hospital, in Tuscaloosa, which treats defendants sent by the criminal courts. In August 2025, 273 men were waiting for a bed.
def: Taylor Hardin Secure Medical Facility is the state's forensic psychiatric hospital, in Tuscaloosa: it treats defendants found incompetent to stand trial and others committed through the criminal courts
. Its waiting list stood at 273 men in an August 2025 court filing, up from approximately 60 in 2017
. The wait is the subject of a 2018 consent decree
. The press reports that give these figures give state totals and name no north Alabama county

short: Care delivered at a distance by video or telephone.
def: Telehealth is care delivered at a distance by video or telephone

. Alabama's manual for Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinics expects a clinic to use telehealth, video conferencing and other technologies as far as possible, in line with the preferences of the person served, to support access to required services
. During the school closures of spring 2020 WellStone delivered school-based therapy by phone and video
. Cullman Regional's 2025 implementation plan for mental health does not mention telehealth
. Census figures show 92.3% of Madison County households and 87.3% of Cullman County households with a broadband internet subscription

short: This report's name for Madison and Cullman counties, the two counties for which WellStone is the community mental health center.
def: "The core" is this report's own label for Madison and Cullman counties, the only two that the Department of Mental Health assigns to WellStone as their community mental health center
. Their combined population in the Census Bureau's estimates for 1 July 2025 was 527,525: 433,516 in Madison County and 94,009 in Cullman County
. The four local governments that appoint WellStone's board are all in these two counties

short: A Cullman nonprofit that works against poverty. It runs a food pantry, won a 2020 federal grant for a reentry program for people leaving jail or prison, and is an accredited family resource center.
def: The Link of Cullman County has served the county since 2013, with a stated mission of helping people grow out of poverty through encouragement, education and employability training
. Its food pantry serves 800 households a month
. In 2020 it received a $500,000 federal Second Chance Act grant for a reentry program, working with the sheriff and taking referrals from the state parole bureau
. Cullman Regional names it among its mental health partners, and in September 2026 it became Alabama's 28th accredited family resource center

short: This report's name for the thirteen counties, beyond Madison and Cullman, that the state assigns to the Huntsville crisis center.
def: "The ring" is this report's label for the thirteen counties that the Department of Mental Health lists, with Madison and Cullman, as served by the Huntsville crisis center: Cherokee, DeKalb, Etowah, Fayette, Jackson, Lamar, Lawrence, Limestone, Marion, Marshall, Morgan, Walker and Winston
. One Department page calls them the "surrounding counties"
. For routine care they belong to four other community mental health centers
. Summed from the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimates they hold 792,981 people, against 527,525 in the core

short: How long a new patient waits: days to an initial evaluation and days to a first therapy session. It is one of the measures a certified clinic must report.
def: Time to services is one of the five quality measures a Certified Community Behavioral Health Clinic must collect itself

. For WellStone, the Alabama Department of Mental Health told legislators in January 2026 that days to an initial evaluation fell from 18 in January 2025 to less than one in December 2025, and days to a first therapy session from 33 to eight
. These four numbers are the only access-time figures published for WellStone

term: TRAM (Transportation for Rural Areas of Madison County)
short: Madison County's rural public transport outside Huntsville: a weekday service on which a ride must be booked a day ahead.
def: TRAM, Transportation for Rural Areas of Madison County, is the county's rural demand-response service

. The Alabama Department of Public Health's list gives its hours as Monday to Thursday 6:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and Friday 6:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., with rides booked 24 hours in advance and before 3 p.m. the day before
. The Alabama Department of Transportation's 2023 study records different hours, Monday to Friday 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., along with 7 drivers and 10 vehicles

short: Care a provider delivers and is not paid for. WellStone reports nearly $3.4 million for fiscal year 2025; the Huntsville Hospital system's audit gives about $144.4 million.
def: The Huntsville Hospital system's audit defines uncompensated care as charity care, uncollectible accounts and uncompensated Medicaid and Medicare care to the indigent
. It puts the total at about $144.4 million for the year ended June 2025, down from about $171.4 million, a fall it attributes mainly to higher Medicaid access payments
. WellStone says it provided nearly $3.4 million in uncompensated care in fiscal year 2025, and its annual report for fiscal year 2021 gave $3.5 million
. WellStone also states that no one is turned away because of inability to pay

short: The share of people with no health insurance. Two versions appear here: people under 65 (8.3% in Madison, 11.9% in Cullman) and all ages in 2024 (7.72% and 10.9%).
def: Census QuickFacts reports the share of people under 65 with no health insurance: 8.3% in Madison County and 11.9% in Cullman County
. Census survey estimates for 2024 covering all ages, as an aggregator presents them, give 7.72% for Madison County and 10.9% for Cullman County
. Inside Madison County the under-65 figure is 10.6% in the city of Huntsville and 4.4% in the city of Madison
. In the ring it runs from 8.4% in Limestone County to 14.6% in DeKalb County

short: A 20-bed psychiatric hospital in Huntsville giving inpatient care to people aged 55 and older.
def: Unity Psychiatric Care in Huntsville is a 20-bed hospital offering inpatient care for people 55 and older, at 5315 Millennium Drive NW
. Huntsville Hospital's own behavioral health page describes inpatient care for adults and seniors and gives no bed count
. In Cullman County the hospital association's listing for Cullman Regional Medical Center shows outpatient psychiatric services only

short: The federal Department of Veterans Affairs' own sites for veterans. Huntsville has an outpatient clinic and a Vet Center; no VA site is listed in Cullman County.
def: The VA, the federal Department of Veterans Affairs, runs health care for eligible veterans separately from the state system, and its Vet Centers are small community sites that offer counseling
. Its Birmingham system lists three sites in Huntsville, one of them inside Fox Army Health Center, and none in Cullman, Decatur or Madison
. The Huntsville VA Clinic at 500 Markaview Road NW is an outpatient clinic offering mental health consultation, evaluation and treatment

. The Huntsville Vet Center at 415 Church Street offers free, confidential counseling for depression, post-traumatic stress disorder and military sexual trauma, with no requirement to be enrolled in VA care

short: The state program that helps people with disabilities prepare for and find work, run by the Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services.
def: Vocational rehabilitation is the state program, run by the Alabama Department of Rehabilitation Services, that helps people with disabilities prepare for and find work
. Its Huntsville office serves Madison and Jackson counties
. Cullman County is served from the Decatur office, together with Lawrence, Limestone and Morgan counties

variants: Mental Health Center of Madison County
short: The nonprofit community mental health center for Madison and Cullman counties. It also runs the Huntsville crisis center, a 988 call center and a pediatric crisis unit.
def: WellStone is the community mental health center that the Department of Mental Health assigns to Madison and Cullman counties, and to no others; it also runs the Huntsville crisis center and pediatric crisis unit and one of Alabama's four in-state 988 call centers
. It says it was incorporated in 1969 under Act 310 of 1967, was known for more than 25 years as the Mental Health Center of Madison County, and took the WellStone name in 2014
. The Cullman Area Mental Health Authority merged into it on 1 October 2017
. An 18-member board governs it: six members appointed by the City of Huntsville, six by the Madison County Commission, three by the City of Cullman and three by the Cullman County Commission
. Its plan says it served over 12,000 people in the two counties in fiscal year 2025, and the Department's tables for that year give 11,659 and 13,700

short: WellStone's adult crisis center on Memorial Parkway in Huntsville. Its permanent building opened in September 2022, and the state assigns it fifteen counties.
def: WellStone Emergency Services is the crisis center at 4020 Memorial Parkway SW in Huntsville, which the Department of Mental Health lists together with WellStone Pediatric Crisis Care as serving fifteen counties
. A temporary center opened in May 2021, and the permanent 25,000-square-foot building, reported to cost $10 million, opened in September 2022
. It was built for up to 15 temporary observation beds and up to 24 extended observation beds, starting with 16
. The Department counts 1,879 people served there in fiscal year 2025, and WellStone's plan says the center has over 150 admissions a month

short: The two-year plan WellStone files with the Department of Mental Health. The current one, signed on 18 November 2025, names its service area, people served and unmet needs.
def: WellStone's strategic plan for fiscal years 2026 and 2027 was signed by its board president on 18 November 2025 and posted on the Department of Mental Health's website in January 2026
. The plan is produced every two years, with needs assessed through written surveys and face-to-face discussions
. It names three unmet needs: adequate housing options for clients, funding for medications for adult clients with no third-party reimbursement, and recruiting and retaining a nursing workforce
. Its four goals concern financial stability, customer experience, business processes and the number of clinicians certified in evidence-based treatments
. It lists its funding sources without amounts

short: Medically supervised withdrawal from alcohol or drugs in a staffed unit, often called detox. WellStone's River Crossing unit in Huntsville has 16 beds.
def: Withdrawal management is medically supervised withdrawal from alcohol or drugs, more often called detox; it is the first step of treatment and not the whole of it

. WellStone won the Alabama Department of Mental Health's request for proposals for a 16-bed residential program for adults with an opioid, benzodiazepine or alcohol use disorder, and opened it in Huntsville as River Crossing on 24 June 2025
. The Department says the beds are funded through a grant from the state's Opioid Settlement Fund
. Its provider directory lists the unit for Madison County as the River Crossing Residential Withdrawal Management Program
. Bradford Health Services' Madison campus also advertises on-site medical detox
